For \(n \ge 1\) and \(\operatorname{Re}s > 1\), \(\int_1^\infty (x/n - 1)_+ \, x^{-s-1} \, d x = n^{-s}/\bigl(s(s-1)\bigr)\).
\(S(x) = x \int_1^x \psi(t) \, t^{-2} \, d t\). Hence \(G(x) \ll x \log x\) for \(x \ge 2\).

For \(\operatorname{Re}s > 1\), \[\begin{equation} \label{eq:F}\tag{2} F(s) := \int_1^\infty G(x)\, x^{-s-1} \, d x = -\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(s) \, \frac{1}{s(s-1)} - \frac{1}{(s-1)^2} + \frac{1 + \gamma}{s - 1} . \end{equation}\]

\(F\) is meromorphic in \(\mathbb{C}\) and regular at \(s = 1\). Its poles in \(\operatorname{Re}s > 0\) are the zeros \(\rho\) of \(\zeta\) in the critical strip \(0 \le \operatorname{Re}s \le 1\), and a zero of multiplicity \(m\) gives residue \(-m/\bigl(\rho(\rho - 1)\bigr)\).
The residue of \(F(s) x^s\) at \(s = 0\) is \(\log 2\pi\).

For \(x > 1\), \[G(x) = \log 2\pi - \sum_\rho \frac{x^\rho}{\rho(\rho - 1)} + O(x^{-2}) ,\] where \(\rho\) runs over the zeros of \(\zeta\) in the critical strip with multiplicity, and the sum converges absolutely.
If the Riemann hypothesis holds, then \(\lvert G(x) - \log 2\pi \rvert \le (2 + \gamma - \log 4\pi)\sqrt{x} + O(x^{-2})\).

Let \(\rho = \beta + i\gamma_0\) be a nonreal zero of \(\zeta\), and let \(c := -1/\bigl(\rho(\rho-1)\bigr)\). The joint term \(c x^\rho + \bar c x^{\bar\rho}\) of \(\rho\) and \(\bar\rho\) in Theorem 1.1.1 exceeds \(\lvert c \rvert x^\beta\) for all \(x\) in a set whose image under \(\log\) has density \(1/3\) in \([0, \infty)\), and it is less than \(-\lvert c \rvert x^\beta\) on another such set.
In this situation \(H(\sigma)\) is bounded below for real \(\sigma \in (\sigma_c, \sigma_c + 1]\).
If \(\sigma_c > \theta\), then \(\sigma_c\) is a real zero of \(\zeta\), and \(H(\sigma) \to -\infty\) as \(\sigma \downarrow \sigma_c\). Hence \(\sigma_c \le \theta\).
Let \(0 < \theta < 1\). If \(G(x) \le x^\theta\) for all large \(x\), then \(\zeta\) has no zeros in \(\operatorname{Re}s > \theta\).
If for every \(\varepsilon > 0\) one has \(G(x) \le x^{1/2 + \varepsilon}\) for all large \(x\), then the Riemann hypothesis holds.

For \(0<\alpha<1\), \(t>0\), \(\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha\): \(\int_1^\infty x^{\alpha-1}(1 + \cos(t\log x))x^{-s}dx = \frac1{s-\alpha} + \frac{1/2}{s-\alpha-it} + \frac{1/2}{s-\alpha+it}\); at \((\alpha, t, s) = (0.3, 2, 1.1)\) both give \(1.42241\ldots\). For real \(s\) the integrand is \(\ge0\); the poles \(\alpha \pm it\) lie beside \(\alpha\).

Let \(E \colon \mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}\) and \(r \colon \mathbb{C}\to \mathbb{C}\). Suppose that \(E\) is Borel measurable, and that there are \(C \in \mathbb{R}\) and a meromorphic function \(\Phi\) on \(\mathbb{C}\) such that \(\lvert E(v) \rvert \le C e^v\) for all \(v \ge 0\), such that \(\Phi(s) = \int_0^\infty E(v) e^{(1-s)v} \, d v\) for all \(s\) with \(\operatorname{Re}s > 2\), and such that \((z - \rho)\Phi(z) \to r(\rho)\) as \(z \to \rho\), \(z \ne \rho\), for every \(\rho\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\rho > 0\). Let \(\beta > 0\). Suppose that \(\operatorname{Re}r(x) \ge 0\) for every real \(x > \beta\), and that there is \(V\) with \(E(v) \le e^{(\beta - 1)v}\) for all \(v \ge V\). Then \(r(\rho) = 0\) for every \(\rho \in \mathbb{C}\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\rho > \beta\).

\(\lambda(n) = \varphi(q)^{-1} \sum_\psi \bigl(\psi(n) - \psi(n)\chi_d(n)\bigr) \Lambda(n)\), and \(0 \le \lambda(n) \le 2\Lambda(n)\). For \(q = 1\) and \(d = 7\) the nonzero values for \(n \le 11\) are \(\lambda(3) = 2\log 3\), \(\lambda(5) = 2\log 5\) and \(\lambda(7) = \log 7\).

§2.1. Inert primes and a quadratic character

(i) For every prime \(p\), \(\chi_d(p)\) is \(1\), \(-1\) or \(0\) according as \(p\) splits, is inert, or ramifies in \(K\). (ii) For a prime power \(r = p^h\), \(1 - \chi_d(r)\) is \(2\) if \(p\) is inert and \(h\) is odd, \(1\) if \(p = d\), and \(0\) otherwise.
\(S_d(x) - x \log x + (1 + \gamma - c_{\chi_d}) x = G(x) - G_{\chi_d}(x)\).

Let \(0 < \theta < 1\). Suppose that \(L(s, \chi_d)\) has no real zero in \((\theta, 1)\), and that \(G(x) - G_{\chi_d}(x) \le x^\theta\) for all large \(x\). Then every zero of \(\zeta(s)\) or of \(L(s, \chi_d)\) in \(\operatorname{Re}s > \theta\) is a zero of both, with the same multiplicity.

Let \(0 < \theta < \beta\) and \(t_0 \ge 0\). Suppose that \(L(s, \chi_d) \ne 0\) on \(\mathcal{B}(\beta, t_0)\), and that \(G(x) - G_{\chi_d}(x) \le x^\theta\) for all large \(x\). Then \(\zeta\) has no zero in \(\mathcal{B}(\beta, t_0)\).
Let \(d \equiv 7 \pmod 8\). Then \(\chi_d(2) = 1\) and \(\chi_d(-1) = -1\). Hence \(2\) splits in \(K\), \(1 - \chi_d(r)\) vanishes at every power of \(2\), and \(\chi_d\) is an odd character.

(i) Let \(\chi\) be a nonprincipal character modulo \(q\) of parity \(j\). For \(\operatorname{Re}s > 0\) the integral \(\int_0^\infty \Theta_\chi(u)\, u^{s - 1/2}\, du/u\) converges absolutely and equals \(\Gamma_j(s) L(s, \chi)\). For \(\chi = \chi_7\), \(j = 1\) and \(s = 1\) its value is \(1/(2\sqrt 7) = 0.18898\ldots\) (ii) For every character \(\chi\) and \(\operatorname{Re}s > 1\), \(\int_0^\infty \Theta_{\chi\mu}(u)\, u^{s - 1/2}\, du/u = \Gamma_j(s)/L(s, \chi)\).

Let \(\chi\) be a primitive nonprincipal character modulo \(q\) of parity \(j\). Then \(\lvert \Theta_\chi(1/(q u)) \rvert = \lvert \Theta_\chi(u) \rvert\) for \(u > 0\). Hence the integrals of \(\lvert \Theta_\chi(u) \rvert\, du/u\) over \(u < q^{-1/2}\) and over \(u > q^{-1/2}\) are equal.

(i) \(\sum_{n \ge 1} \lvert w_j(n u) \rvert \le 3 e^{-u}/u\) for \(u > 0\). (ii) For every character \(\chi\), every \(T > 0\) and \(\operatorname{Re}z = 2\): \(\lvert \Gamma_j(z)/L(z, \chi) - \mathcal{M}_T(z) \rvert \le 3/T\) and \(\lvert \Gamma_j(z) L(z, \chi) \rvert \le 3\), so \(\lvert \Phi(z) \rvert \le 9/T\).

Let \(\chi\) be a primitive nonprincipal character modulo \(q\) of parity \(j\), and \(T > 0\) with \(q \le T^2\). On \(\operatorname{Re}z = \frac12\): \(\lvert \Gamma_j(z) L(z, \chi) \rvert \le 2 J(\chi, T)\) and \(\lvert \mathcal{M}_T(z) \rvert \le J(\chi, T)\).

There is a constant \(C_j\) with the following property. Let \(\delta > 0\) and \(T > 0\), and let \(\chi\) be a primitive nonprincipal character modulo \(q\) of parity \(j\), with \(q \le T^2\) and \(J(\chi, T) \le T^{2\delta}\). If \(L(s, \chi) = 0\) and \(\frac12 + 9\delta \le \operatorname{Re}s \le 1\), then \(\lvert \Gamma_j(s) \rvert^2 \le C_j T^{-2\delta}\).

Let \(\delta > 0\) and \(t_0 \in \mathbb{R}\). For all \(T\) large in terms of \(\delta\) and \(t_0\) the following holds for every \(q\) and every primitive nonprincipal character \(\chi\) modulo \(q\) of parity \(j\) with \(q \le T^2\): if \(L(s, \chi)\) vanishes somewhere on \(\mathcal{B}(\frac12 + 9\delta, t_0)\), then \(J(\chi, T) > T^{2\delta}\).

Let \(d \equiv 7 \pmod 8\) be prime. For every \(n \ge 1\), \(\bigl(\tfrac{n}{d}\bigr) = \bigl(\tfrac{-d}{n^\circ}\bigr)\). For instance \(\bigl(\tfrac{12}{7}\bigr) = \bigl(\tfrac{-7}{3}\bigr) = -1\).

Let \(\delta > 0\) and \(n \ge 1\), and suppose that \(n^\circ\) is not a square. Then \(v \mapsto \bigl(\tfrac{-v}{n^\circ}\bigr)\) is \(\pm 1\) times a nonprincipal character modulo \(n^\circ\), and \(\bigl\lvert \sum_{1 \le v \le X} \bigl(\tfrac{-v}{n^\circ}\bigr) \bigr\rvert \le C_\delta\, n^{1/2 + \delta/2}\) for every \(X\), with \(C_\delta\) depending only on \(\delta\).
Let \(\delta > 0\). For \(u > 0\), \(\sum \lvert w_j(n u)\, w_j(n' u) \rvert \le C_\delta\, u^{-1 - 2\delta}\), the sum over the pairs \(n, n' \ge 1\) with \((n n')^\circ\) a square.

Let \(\delta > 0\), \(T > 0\) and \(u \ge 1/T\). Then \(\sum_{1 \le v \le T^2} \lvert \Theta_{c_v}(u) \rvert^2 \le C_\delta\, T^2 u^{-2\delta}\), with \(C_\delta\) depending only on \(\delta\) and \(j\), not on \(\alpha\), \(T\) or \(u\).

Let \(\delta > 0\). For \(T > 0\) and every \(\alpha\) with \(\lvert \alpha(n) \rvert \le 1\), \(\sum_{1 \le v \le T^2} J(c_v, T) \le C_\delta\, T^{2 + \delta}\), with \(C_\delta\) depending only on \(\delta\) and \(j\).

Let \(\delta > 0\) and \(t_0 \ge 0\). For all large \(X\), at most \(C X^{1 - \delta/2}\) primes \(d \le X\) with \(d \equiv 7 \pmod 8\) have a zero of \(L(s, \chi_d)\) on \(\mathcal{B}(\frac12 + 9\delta, t_0)\); here \(C\) depends on \(\delta\) and \(t_0\).
For every \(\beta > \frac12\) and \(t_0 \ge 0\) there are infinitely many primes \(d \equiv 7 \pmod 8\) with \(L(s, \chi_d) \ne 0\) on \(\mathcal{B}(\beta, t_0)\).

Let \(d \equiv 7 \pmod 8\) be prime, \(\xi\) a character modulo \(8\), and \(\xi^*\) the primitive character inducing \(\xi\), of conductor \(f \in \{1, 4, 8\}\). Then \(\xi^*\chi_d\) is primitive modulo \(fd\); \(L(s, \xi\chi_d) = (1 - 2^{-s}) L(s, \chi_d)\) if \(\xi\) is principal, and \(L(s, \xi\chi_d) = L(s, \xi^*\chi_d)\) otherwise. Hence for \(\beta > 0\) the four twists have no zero on \(\mathcal{B}(\beta, t_0)\) exactly when the four \(L(s, \xi^*\chi_d)\) have none.

Let \(N \ge 1\), \(\delta > 0\) and \(t_0 \in \mathbb{R}\), and let \(a \in \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}\) be a class such that every prime \(p \equiv a \pmod N\) satisfies \(p \equiv 7 \pmod 8\) and \(\gcd(N, p) = 1\). Call a prime \(d \equiv a \pmod N\) bad if for some character \(\xi\) modulo \(N\) the function \(L(s, \xi\chi_d)\) vanishes at some \(s\) with \(\operatorname{Re}s \ge \frac12 + 9\delta\) and \(\lvert \operatorname{Im}s \rvert \le t_0\). Then the number of bad primes \(d \le X\) is \(O(X^{1 - \delta/2})\) as \(X \to \infty\) through the positive integers.

Let \(N \ge 1\), \(\beta > \frac12\) and \(t_0 \in \mathbb{R}\), and let \(a\) be a unit of \(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}\) such that every prime \(p \equiv a \pmod N\) satisfies \(p \equiv 7 \pmod 8\) and \(\gcd(N, p) = 1\). Then there is a prime \(d \equiv a \pmod N\) such that for every character \(\xi\) modulo \(N\) and every \(s \in \mathbb{C}\) with \(\operatorname{Re}s \ge \beta\) and \(\lvert \operatorname{Im}s \rvert \le t_0\), \(L(s, \xi\chi_d) \ne 0\).

For an integer \(\mu \ge 0\), let \(\mathcal{N}_\mu\) be the set of integers in \([0, 3^\mu)\) whose base-\(3\) digits are \(0\) or \(1\). (i) \(\mathcal{N}_\mu\) contains no nonconstant three-term arithmetic progression, and \(\lvert \mathcal{N}_\mu\rvert = (3^\mu)^{\log 2/\log 3}\). (Local Tate duality and Euler characteristic). At a finite place \(v\), the cup product followed by evaluation \(M\otimes M^*\to\mu\) and the local invariant \(\operatorname{inv}_v\) gives a perfect pairing \[H^1(F_v,M)\times H^1(F_v,M^*)\longrightarrow \mathbb Q/\mathbb Z.\] The orders of the local groups satisfy \[\begin{align} \# H^1(F_v,M)&=\# H^0(F_v,M)\,\# H^2(F_v,M)\,|\#M|_v^{-1},\\ \# H^2(F_v,M)&=\# H^0(F_v,M^*). \end{align}\] The absolute value \(|\cdot|_v\) gives a uniformizer absolute value \((\#k_v)^{-1}\), where \(k_v\) is the residue field.

(Unramified classes). At a finite place, \[\#H^1_{\mathrm{ur}}(F_v,M)=\#H^0(F_v,M).\] If inertia acts trivially on \(M\) and the residue characteristic is prime to \(\#M\), then \(H^1_{\mathrm{ur}}(F_v,M)\) and \(H^1_{\mathrm{ur}}(F_v,M^*)\) are exact annihilators.

A family of local conditions \(\mathcal L\) consists of subgroups \(\mathcal L_v\subseteq H^1(F_v,M)\), equal to \(H^1_{\mathrm{ur}}(F_v,M)\) at all but finitely many finite places. Write \(\mathcal L_v^\perp\) for the annihilator under the local pairing. The Selmer group \(H^1_{\mathcal L}(F,M)\) is the group of classes whose restriction at each \(v\) lies in \(\mathcal L_v\). Use the same definition for \(H^1_{\mathcal L^\perp}(F,M^*)\).

(Greenberg–Wiles). For local conditions \(\mathcal L\) as above, the two Selmer groups are finite and \[\frac{\#H^1_{\mathcal L}(F,M)}{\#H^1_{\mathcal L^\perp}(F,M^*)} = \frac{\#H^0(F,M)}{\#H^0(F,M^*)} \prod_v \frac{\#\mathcal L_v}{\#H^0(F_v,M)} .\] Here \(H^0\) means ordinary invariants, including at infinite places.

(Reciprocity). For a class in \(H^2(F,\mu)\), the sum of the local invariants is zero. Let \(n\ge 1\) and write \(\mu_n\) for the \(n\)-th roots of unity. At a finite place \(v\), let \(\chi\) be a continuous character of \(G_{F_v}\) into \(\tfrac1n\mathbb Z/\mathbb Z\) and \([a]\) the Kummer class of \(a\in F_v^\times\) in \(H^1(F_v,\mu_n)\). Then \[\operatorname{inv}_v(\chi\cup[a])=\chi(\operatorname{rec}_v(a)).\] The coefficient pairing sends \((j/n,\xi)\) to \(\xi^j\) for \(\xi\in\mu_n\). The local Artin map \(\operatorname{rec}_v\) sends a uniformizer to arithmetic Frobenius modulo inertia. In particular, if \(\chi\) is unramified, the invariant is \(\operatorname{ord}_v(a)\chi(\mathrm{Fr}_v)\), where \(\operatorname{ord}_v\) gives a uniformizer value \(1\).
The group of cube roots of unity in \(\mathbb Q_q\) has order \(1\) at \(q=5\) and \(3\) at \(q=7,13,19\).
The order of \(H^1(\mathbb Q_q,\mathbb Z/3)\) is \(3\) at \(q=5\) and \(9\) at \(q=7,13,19\).

For any finite place \(v\) of \(\mathbb Q\), the annihilator of the unramified subgroup of \(H^1(\mathbb Q_v,\mathbb Z/3)\) consists of Kummer classes represented by elements of valuation divisible by \(3\).
The dual Selmer group is trivial.
Inflation identifies \(\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb Q(\mu_q)/\mathbb Q),\mathbb Z/3)\) with the Selmer group.
The Selmer group has order \(1\) at \(q=5\) and \(3\) at \(q=7,13,19\). For each of the latter primes the nonzero characters cut out the unique cubic subfield of \(\mathbb Q(\mu_q)\).
Both sides of Theorem 33.1.3 are \(1,3,3,3\) in the order \(q=5,7,13,19\). The real place contributes a factor of \(1/3\) to the product.

(Chebotarev, existence form). Let a nonempty subset of \(G_F\) be a neighborhood of each of its points, and prescribe a finite set of finite places of \(F\) to avoid. An arithmetic Frobenius element is a lift to the decomposition group of the map \(x\mapsto x^{\#k_v}\) on the residue field of the chosen place.

§34.5. A chart for a Tate twist

A lattice \(L\) is crystalline if the fixed vectors of \(G_{F_v}\) in \(B_{\max}\otimes_{\mathbb Z_\ell}L\) span over \(B_{\max}\). It is potentially crystalline if the restriction to the Galois group of a finite extension of \(F_v\) is crystalline. Here \(B_{\max}\) is Colmez’s crystalline period ring. Fontaine’s ring \(B_{\mathrm{cris}}\) gives the same conditions, using \(\varphi(B_{\max})\subseteq B_{\mathrm{cris}}\subseteq B_{\max}\) for the Galois-equivariant Frobenius \(\varphi\) [Fo; Co].

A lattice is Hodge–Tate if \(\mathbb C_\ell\otimes_{\mathbb Z_\ell} L\) is a direct sum of twists \(\mathbb C_\ell(e)=\mathbb C_\ell\otimes_{\mathbb Z_\ell}\mathbb Z_\ell(e)\) as a semilinear representation. A summand \(\mathbb C_\ell(e)\) contributes one jump \(u=-e\). In particular \(\mathbb Z_\ell(e)\) has jump \(-e\).
The module \(Z_f(L)\) consists of maps \(c\colon G_{F_v}\to L\) for which there is a \(y\in B_{\max}\otimes_{\mathbb Z_\ell}L\) with \(1\otimes c(g)=gy-y\) for every \(g\in G_{F_v}\).

(Rank of crystalline cocycles). Suppose \(L\) is potentially crystalline. Then \(Z_f(L)\) is a saturated submodule of \(Z^1(F_v,L)\) and is finite free over \(\mathbb Z_\ell\). If \(n^-\) is the number of negative jumps, counted with multiplicity, then \[\operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Z_\ell} Z_f(L)=\operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Z_\ell} L+[F_v:\mathbb Q_\ell]n^- .\]

For \(L=\mathbb Z_\ell(e)\) the ranks of \(Z_f(L)\), for \(e<0\), \(e=0\) and \(e>0\), are \(1,1,1+[F_v:\mathbb Q_\ell]\), respectively. The corresponding dimensions of \(H^1_f(F_v,\mathbb Q_\ell(e))\) are \(0,1,[F_v:\mathbb Q_\ell]\).
The group \(Z_f(\mathbb Z_\ell)\) consists of the unramified homomorphisms, with one free parameter given by the value on arithmetic Frobenius.

Take \(F_v=\mathbb Q_\ell\), \(\ell\) odd and \(e<0\). Put \(n_0=0\) if \((\ell-1)\nmid e\) and \(n_0=1+\operatorname{val}_\ell(e)\) otherwise, with \(\operatorname{val}_\ell(\ell)=1\). In a basis of \(\mathbb Z_\ell(e)\) the function \[g\longmapsto \frac{\chi_{\mathrm{cyc}}(g)^e-1}{\ell^{n_0}}\] generates \(Z_f(\mathbb Z_\ell(e))\). The coboundaries have index \(\ell^{n_0}\). For \((\ell,e)=(5,-4)\) and \((5,-20)\) the indices are \(5\) and \(25\).

For potentially crystalline \(L\) and \(n\ge 1\), the kernel of \(\mathrm{red}_n\) on \(Z_f(L)\) is \(\ell^n Z_f(L)\). Consequently \(\#\mathrm{red}_n Z_f(L)=\ell^{n\operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Z_\ell} Z_f(L)}\).

Let \(L\) be potentially crystalline and \(n\ge 1\). A jump \(u\) of \(L\) corresponds to a jump \(-u-1\) of its Tate dual, with the same multiplicity. Exactly one of the two integers is negative, and \[\#\mathrm{red}_n Z_f(L)\,\#\mathrm{red}_n Z_f(L^*(1)) =\lvert L/\ell^nL\rvert^{\,2+[F_v:\mathbb Q_\ell]} .\] For a Tate twist over \(\mathbb Q_\ell\) the product is \(\ell^{3n}\) for every \(e\).

(Crystalline local duality). Let \(L\) be potentially crystalline, let \(L'=L^*(1)\), and put \(V'=L'\otimes_{\mathbb Z_\ell}\mathbb Q_\ell\). In the local Tate pairing of \(H^1(F_v,L)\) with \(H^1(F_v,V'/L')\), the subgroup \(H^1_f(F_v,L)\) and the image of \(H^1_f(F_v,V')\) are exact annihilators.

The reductions modulo \(\ell\) of \(Z_f(\mathbb Z_\ell)\) and \(Z_f(\mathbb Z_\ell(1))\) are exact annihilators for the pairing of \(Z^1(\mathbb Q_\ell,M)\) and \(Z^1(\mathbb Q_\ell,\mu_\ell)\) induced by cup product and the local invariant. (Breuil–Kisin modules). Choose a uniformizer \(\varpi_v\) of \(F_v\) with compatible \(\ell\)-power roots. With \(d_l=(\int_G|\mathsf c_l(g)|^2\,dg)^{-1}\), for \(x,y\in G\) one has \[d_l\int_G \mathsf c_l(xgy)\overline{\mathsf c_l(g)}\,dg=\mathsf c_l(x)\mathsf c_l(y), \qquad d_l=\mathrm{ch}_l(1)= \frac{\prod_{l_i>l_j}(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)}{\prod_{a=0}^{n-1}a!}.\]

(Flensted-Jensen’s formula). For an integer weight \(\mathbf w=(w_i)\) and an invertible matrix \(g\), let \(m_{\mathbf w}(g)\) be the product over integers \(s\) of the determinant of the submatrix on rows and columns \(\{i:w_i\ge s\}\), with each factor for \(s\le0\) divided by \(\det g\). The empty minor is \(1\) and only finitely many factors differ from \(1\). For \(g\in G\), keep the two same-sign diagonal blocks of \(g\) and set the other blocks to zero to obtain an invertible matrix \(D_g\). With \(z=D_g^{-1}g\), the integral formula is \[\mathsf c_l(g)= \frac{\displaystyle\int_K \frac{m_\Lambda(D_g k)\overline{m_\Lambda(k)}}{m_{-\lambda-\rho}(k^*zk)} \,dk} {\displaystyle\int_K |m_\Lambda(k)|^2\,dk},\] where \(k^*\) is the conjugate transpose.

(Decay). If \(l\) has gap at least \(h\), then for each integer \(0\le c\le h\) and each \(g\in G\), \[|\mathsf c_l(g)|\le (2/\|g\|_{\mathrm{op}})^c ,\] with the Euclidean operator norm. In particular \(|\mathsf c_l(g)|\le 1\).

(Character on the diagonal torus). Let \(x=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\) have distinct entries \(t_i\) of modulus one. In this chapter set \(\mathsf k_i=(l_i+n-1)/2\). Write \(A_K(\mathsf k)(x)\) for the alternating sum of the monomial \(\prod_i t_i^{\mathsf k_i}\) over permutations preserving the signs. The character \(\mathrm{Ch}_l\) of \(\pi_l\) on the regular diagonal torus satisfies \[\mathrm{ch}_l(1)\int_G\mathsf c_l(g^{-1}xg)\,dg = \mathrm{Ch}_l(x) = (-1)^{pq}\frac{A_K(\mathsf k)(x)}{\prod_{l_i>l_j}(t_i-t_j)} .\] Define the kernel \(\mathsf e_l=d_l\overline{\mathsf c_l}\). The proof gives absolute convergence for the integral coefficient at the gap of the sum.

For an integer \(j\ge 0\), the normalized coefficient of the vector \(e_1^{\otimes j}\) in \(\mathrm{Sym}^j\mathbb C^2\) is \(g_{11}^j\), with \(e_1=(1,0)\) and the inner product induced from tensor powers of \(\mathbb C^2\). In the compact chart take \(|z|=\tan t\), \(0\le t<\pi/2\). Probability measure has radial density \(\sin(2t)\,dt\). In the disk take \(|z|=\tanh t\), the radius of \(a_t[0:1]\). The compact-dual measure has radial density \(\sinh(2t)\,dt\).

The pullback of half-plane area \(dx\,dy/y^2\) under \(z\mapsto \mathrm{i}(1+z)/(1-z)\) is \(4\pi\) times the compact-dual quotient measure on the disk. The rescaled degree is \((\mathsf N-1)/(4\pi)\). For even \(\mathsf N\ge4\) the result agrees with Problem 10.5.5 at weight \(\mathsf N\).

For \(g=k a_t k'\) with \(k,k'\in K\), the coefficient in Problem 41.1.3 has modulus \(\cosh(t)^{-\mathsf N}\), and \(\|g\|_{\mathrm{op}}=e^t\). In particular \(|\mathsf c_l(g)|\le (2/\|g\|_{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathsf N}\).

For signs \((+,-)\) and \(\mathsf k_1>\mathsf k_2\), write \(\mathrm{Ch}(t_1,t_2)=t_1^{\mathsf k_1}t_2^{\mathsf k_2}/(t_2-t_1)\) for the character in Theorem 41.5 at distinct unit entries. Let \(\pi\) be an irreducible unitary representation of a finite group \(G_0\), of dimension \(d_\pi\), and \(u\) a unit vector. For \(\mathsf c(g)=\langle u,\pi(g)u\rangle\), one has \[\frac{d_\pi}{\#G_0}\sum_{g\in G_0}\mathsf c(g^{-1}xg)=\operatorname{tr}\pi(x)\quad(x\in G_0).\]

(Selberg principle). Let \(\phi\) be a locally constant compactly supported function on \(G_f\). The orbital integral is zero if the characteristic polynomial over \(E\) is irreducible and has a root off the unit circle under the embedding selected by the CM type at some infinite place.

(Comparison of traces). With \(E\), \(V\) and \(l_\tau\) as in the setup for this section, suppose that \(E\) contains the \(5040\)th roots of unity and has an even number of infinite places. \(V'\) is a framed space of the same rank over \(E\), and the parameters \(l_\tau\) meet the same gap condition for the signs of \(V'\). \(K_f\) is a subgroup of the integral elements of \(G_f\) containing a neighbourhood of the identity, and \(a\in\mathbb C[G_f]\) preserves \(K_f\)-fixed vectors in every representation of \(G_f\). The function \(\phi=a\star 1_{K_f}\) is cuspidal at a split place \(w\). Here \(\star 1_{K_f}\) sends each \(b\in G_f\) to \(1_{bK_f}\) and extends linearly. For cuspidality, let \(P\) be the coordinate projection onto any nonempty proper coordinate subset and let \(\bar b\in\mathrm{GL}_n(k_w)\), where \(k_w\) is the residue field. For each matrix \(A\in M_n(k_w)\) take any integral invertible lift \(u_A\) of \((1+PA(1-P))\bar b\), viewed in \(G_f\) with inverse conjugate transpose at the conjugate place and identity components elsewhere. For every choice of lifts and every \(g\in G_f\), the sum of \(\phi(gu_A)\) over \(A\) is zero. Then the operators induced by \(a\) through right translation have equal traces on the spaces of forms for \(V\) and \(V'\). The spaces are defined as for principal forms in Section 37.4, using level \(K_f\) and the real kernels of the parameters \(l_\tau\) for the respective signs.
(Landherr’s theorem). Hermitian spaces for a quadratic extension of number fields that are isometric at each completion of the base field are isometric over the extension.

For \(w\in\mathbb R\) and \(y>0\), \[\mathsf c(n(w)a(y))=y^{k/2}\bigl((1+y-\mathrm iw)/2\bigr)^{-k}.\] Also \(\mathsf c(1)=1\) and \(\mathsf c(g^{-1})=\overline{\mathsf c(g)}\).

At \(g=a(y)\) the average is \[\frac{(4\pi)^k(yy_0)^{k/2}m^{k-1}}{(k-1)!} e^{-2\pi m(y+y_0)} .\] Check by machine that at \((k,m,y_0,y)=(4,1,0.3,0.5)\) the value is \(0.613576\) to six decimal places.

At \(g=y_*\), the integrand in the coordinate \(u=w/(2y_0)\) is \(Z(u)=(1+\mathrm iu)^{-k}e^{\mathrm is u}\). Its continuous argument vanishing at \(u=0\) has derivative zero there exactly when \(s=k\). At that position, \[|Z(u)|=(1+u^2)^{-k/2},\qquad |\arg Z(u)|\le k|u|^3/3 .\]

At \(s=k\) one has \(P(k)=4\pi k^k e^{-k}/k!\) and \(2y_0\le\sqrt{k}\,W_{y_*}(y_*)\). Check that \(P(k)/\sqrt{8\pi/k}\) is approximately \(0.9595,0.9794,0.99308,0.999167\) for \(k=2,4,12,100\), respectively.

For \(k=12\) they are about \(0.71859\) and \(0.18324\), and for \(k=100\) they are \(0.25045\) and \(0.11321\). For \(k=4\) the right side is about \(-0.0511\).

The period at the identity vanishes. For a real \(\mathsf b\ge0\), let \(I_0=(\sqrt{1+\mathsf b},\sqrt{\mathsf b})^T\) and use the inverse of the real boost with first column \(I_0\) as the position. For a position \(y_*\in G\), the Bessel average at \(v\) is \[W_{y_*,v}(y)=\int_R\mathsf c_\tau(y_*^{-1}sy)\,\pi(s)^{-1}v\,ds .\] The integral converges absolutely for the data, uniformly in the sense that the integral of the norm is bounded as \(y\) varies. §43.2. The Bessel tuple, discriminants and links

Let \(U,U'\) be subgroups of a finite group \(H\) with characters \(\psi,\psi'\), and let \(\phi\colon H\to{\mathbb{C}}\) satisfy \(\phi(ugu')=\psi(u)\phi(g)\psi'(u')\) for \(u\in U\), \(u'\in U'\). If \(ugu'=g\) for some \(u,u'\) with \(\psi(u)\psi'(u')\ne1\), then \(\phi(g)=0\).

In \(\mathrm{GL}_2({\mathbb{F}}_p)\), \(U\operatorname{diag}(t_1,t_2)U\) supports if and only if \(t_1=t_2\), and every double coset in the big cell supports. So \((p-1)+(p-1)^2=p(p-1)\) of the \(2(p-1)^2\) double cosets support: \(6\) of \(8\) for \(p=3\), \(20\) of \(32\) for \(p=5\).

By machine: in \(\mathrm{GL}_3({\mathbb{F}}_2)\), \(4\) of the \(6\) double cosets support, of sizes \(8,32,32,64\) (the two simple reflections do not); in \(\mathrm{GL}_3({\mathbb{F}}_3)\), \(18=2+8+8\) of the \(48\) support, of sizes \(27\), \(243\), \(729\) respectively.

On \({\mathbb{F}}_p^2\) put \(h(y,y'):=y_1y'_2+y_2y'_1\), and for \(g\in\mathrm{GL}_2({\mathbb{F}}_p)\) let \(\langle g\rangle_1:=h(g\mathbf e_1,\mathbf e_1)\). Then \(\langle g\rangle_1=g_{21}\); \({\mathbb{F}}_pg\mathbf e_1={\mathbb{F}}_p\mathbf e_1\) if and only if \(\langle g\rangle_1=0\); and the \(g\) with \(\langle g\rangle_1=0\) whose double coset supports are exactly the scalar multiples of elements of \(U\).

The Bessel tuple is \((v_1,\dots,v_\varrho,v_{\varrho+1})\) with \(v_{\varrho+1}:=z\). For \(\gamma\in U(Y_0)(F)\) the pairing matrix is \(\bigl(h(\gamma v_b,v_a)\bigr)_{1\le a,b\le\varrho+1}\). Its entries are the Bessel pairings. For \(a\le\varrho\), the entry in row \(a\) and column \(b\) is the coefficient of \(v'_a\) in \(\gamma v_b\), and for \(a=\varrho+1\) it is \(-N\) times the coefficient of \(z\). Its leading minors are \(\langle\gamma\rangle_j:=\det\bigl(h(\gamma v_b,v_a)\bigr)_{1\le a,b\le j}\) for \(1\le j\le\varrho+1\), and \(\langle\gamma\rangle_0:=1\).

Define the discriminant of \(\gamma\) by \(\operatorname{disc}(\gamma):=\langle\gamma\rangle_{\varrho+1}\overline{\langle\gamma\rangle_{\varrho+1}}-N^2\langle\gamma\rangle_\varrho\overline{\langle\gamma\rangle_\varrho}\in E\).
Define the link of \(\gamma\) to be the subspace \(\operatorname{lk}(\gamma):=\{([y],[\gamma^{-1}y]):y\perp\mathrm{Fl},\ y\perp\gamma\mathrm{Fl}\}\) of \((X_0\oplus Ez)^2\).

For \(\zeta\in\mathcal O_E\) with \(\zeta\bar\zeta=1\), the scalar coset \(\zeta\bar R_0\) is the set of \(s\in\bar G\) for which some \(t\in\bar R_0\) has \(s_w=(\zeta\bmod w)\,t_w\) for every \(w\in\mathcal M\). A set \(\mathcal B\subseteq\bar G\) avoids the scalar cosets if it meets no \(\zeta\bar R_0\) with \(\zeta\ne1\).

(the terms that survive). If \(\mathcal B\subseteq\bar G\) avoids the scalar cosets and \(s\in\mathcal B\), then for all classes \(c,c'\), for \(W\) and for \(W^\flat\), \[\mathrm{Amp}\bigl(U(Y_0)(F)\smallsetminus R(F);c,s,c'\bigr)=\mathrm{Amp}(\Gamma^*;c,s,c').\]

In a three-dimensional model over \(E\), let \(\varrho=1\) and \(X_0=0\), with basis \(v_1,z,v'_1\), \(h(v_1,v'_1)=1\), \(h(v_1,v_1)=h(v'_1,v'_1)=0\), \(h(z,z)=-N\) and \(z\perp v_1,v'_1\). The two maps \(\gamma_\pm\) exchanging \(v_1\) and \(v'_1\) with \(z\mapsto\pm z\) are isometries of square \(1\) with \(\langle\gamma_\pm\rangle_1=1\), \(\langle\gamma_\pm\rangle_2=\mp N\), \(\operatorname{disc}(\gamma_\pm)=0\) and \(\gamma_\pm\mathrm{Fl}\ne\mathrm{Fl}\); the characters agree on them, whatever the character of \({\mathcal{U}}\), so both lie in \(\Gamma^*\), and \(\operatorname{lk}(\gamma_\pm)\) is spanned by \((z,\pm z)\).

The element \(s\) meets at \(w\) (or at \(\bar w\)) if, modulo that place, the span of the Bessel tuple and the span of its image under \(s\) share a nonzero vector. The meet norm \(\operatorname{mt}(s)\) is the product, over \(w\in\mathcal M\), of a factor \(\#k_w\) if \(s\) meets at \(w\) and a further factor \(\#k_w\) if \(s\) meets at \(\bar w\).

The minor condition holds for \(s\) if at some \(w\in\mathcal M_0\) the leading minors of orders \(1,\dots,\varrho\) of the matrix \(\bigl(h(s_wv_b,v_a)\bigr)_{a,b\le\varrho+1}\), formed with the reduced form, are all nonzero.

Let \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathcal M_0\), and for each \(w\in\mathcal D\) choose \(w\) or \(\bar w\) and a nonzero vector \(y_w\) in the span of the Bessel tuple modulo the chosen place. The fixer of these vectors is the subgroup of the \(s\in\bar G\) whose action modulo the chosen place fixes \(y_w\), for every \(w\in\mathcal D\).

If \(\zeta\in\mathcal O_E\), \(\zeta\bar\zeta=1\) and \(\zeta\equiv1\) modulo every \(w\in\mathcal M_j\), then \(\zeta=1\). For example, in \({\mathbb{Z}}[\mathrm i]\) reduction modulo \(2+\mathrm i\) is injective on \(\mu_4\).

Every fixer contains the reduction of the finite adelic points of \(U(X_0)\) that preserve the lattice, and each element of a fixer meets at the chosen place over every \(w\in\mathcal D\).

(the strip). For the data and \(j=0,1\), \[\sum_{s\in\mathcal B_j}\lVert\mathcal K_s-\rho_{\mathrm{Bes}}(s)\rVert^2\le b^{-12}D_{\mathrm{id}}.\]

Size, congruence saving and count: the remaining terms

Let \(L\subset{\mathbb{C}}^{k'}\) be a lattice of rank \(2k'\) and \(\mathsf h\ge0\) integrable. The mean, for the Haar probability measure on \({\mathbb{C}}^{k'}/L\), of \(\sum_{v\in L}\mathsf h(a+v)\) is \(\int\mathsf h/\operatorname{covol}(L)\). For \(\mathsf h(y)=(1+\lvert y\rvert^2)^{-k'-1}\) it is \(\pi^{k'}/(k'!\operatorname{covol}(L))\); for \(L=(2+\mathrm{i}){\mathbb{Z}}[\mathrm{i}]^2\) it is \(\pi^2/50\approx0.197\).
A lattice of rank \(n'\) in \(\mathbb R^{n'}\) whose inner products are integers has covolume at least \(1\).

Let \(\alpha\in{\mathbb{C}}^\times\), \(y_0\in{\mathbb{C}}^{k'}\) a row, \(A\) a positive definite hermitian matrix of size \(k'\), and \(v:=\alpha y+y_0\) for rows \(y\in{\mathbb{C}}^{k'}\). Then \[\int_{{\mathbb{C}}^{k'}}\det(A+v^*v)^{-k'-1}\,dy=\lvert\alpha\rvert^{-2k'}(\det A)^{-k'}\,\frac{\pi^{k'}}{k'!}.\] For \(k'=7\), \(\alpha=2\), \(A=\operatorname{diag}(3,1,\dots,1)\) the value is \(\pi^7/(7!\,2^{14}3^7)\approx1.672\cdot10^{-8}\).

A set \(\mathfrak S\) of terms is stable if \(u^{-1}\gamma u'\in\mathfrak S\iff\gamma\in\mathfrak S\) for all \(u,u'\in{\mathcal{U}}(F)\). An element \(s\in\bar G\) agrees if the character of \({\mathcal{U}}(\mathbb A_{F,f})\) of the definition of \(\Gamma^*\) in Chapter 43 takes the same value at any two integral \(u,u'\) in it whose reductions satisfy \(\bar us=s\bar u'\).

A term \(\gamma\) has cell rank \(j\in\{0,\dots,\varrho+1\}\) if (i) for some \(\zeta\in E\) with \(\zeta\bar\zeta=1\) and every index \(a\) with \(j<a\le\varrho+1\), some vector \(\sum_{b\le a}x_bv_b=\gamma\sum_{b\le a}y_bv_b\) has \(x_a=\zeta\), \(y_a=1\); (ii) \(\langle\gamma\rangle_j\ne0\); (iii) \(j=\varrho+1\) if and only if \(\operatorname{disc}(\gamma)\ne0\). This rank, when it exists, is unique [GL, BorderedDeterminant.lean, l. 550]. Write it as \(\operatorname{cr}(\gamma)\).

Let \({\mathcal{U}}^0_c\) be the group of the \(u\in{\mathcal{U}}(F)\) that fix every member of the Bessel tuple and have \(h_c^{-1}u_fh_c\in K_M\). The set \(\mathrm{Rep}(\mathfrak S;c,s,c')\) of near representatives of \(\mathfrak S\) over \((c,s,c')\) consists of the \(\gamma\in\mathfrak S\) over \((c,s,c')\) such that \(s\) agrees, \(\gamma\) has a cell rank, \(\gamma\) is the chosen representative of its double coset \({\mathcal{U}}^0_c\gamma\,{\mathcal{U}}^0_{c'}\) [GL, BorderedDeterminant.lean, l. 455], and \(\gamma\) is near: some archimedean point \(y\) has \(y\) and \(\gamma_\infty^{-1}y\) boxed. Use the domain \(D_0\) of [GL, Box.lean, ll. 145, 200], a measurable set of representatives of the tuples \((\mathsf w_\tau)_\tau\) of complex numbers modulo the diagonal image of \(M\mathcal O_E\), with \(\lvert\mathsf w_\tau\rvert\le b^{26}\) on \(D_0\); a point \(y\) is boxed if its Bessel length (Theorem 40.3.1(d)) is at most \(b^{6(\varrho+1)+2}\) at every infinite place and each entry above the diagonal of its Gram–Schmidt matrix in the rational Bessel tuple, as a tuple over the infinite places, lies in \(D_0\) [GL, Setup.lean, ll. 398–423]. A pair of near representatives over \(c,c'\) is a pair \((\gamma,\gamma')\) in \(\mathrm{Rep}(U(Y_0)(F);c,s,c')^2\) for some \(s\).

Let \(\gamma\) lie over a block and have cell rank \(\operatorname{cr}\). Let \(\hat{\mathcal O}_E\) be the ring of integral finite adeles of \(E\). The pairing matrix of \(\tilde\gamma\) has entries given by the Bessel pairings \(h(\tilde\gamma v_b,v_a)\). Let \(I(\gamma)\) be the index, in the \(\hat{\mathcal O}_E\)-module spanned by rows \(a=1,\dots,\varrho\) of this matrix, of the submodule spanned by its first \(\min(\varrho,\operatorname{cr})\) rows, and \(I'(\gamma)\) the same index for \(\tilde\gamma^{-1}\); both are positive [GL, LinkLattice.lean, ll. 457, 464] and equal \(1\) if \(\operatorname{cr}\ge\varrho\), when all \(\varrho\) rows are taken. Define the calibre of \(\gamma\) by \[\operatorname{cal}(\gamma):=M^{2f\min(\varrho,\operatorname{cr})}\,\frac{\max\bigl(N^f\lvert\operatorname{Nm}_{E/\mathbb Q}\langle\gamma\rangle_{\operatorname{cr}}\rvert/N^{2f(\operatorname{cr}-\varrho)_+},\ \prod_\tau\lvert\tau(\operatorname{disc}\gamma)\rvert\bigr)}{I(\gamma)\,I'(\gamma)},\] where \(\tau\) runs over the \(f\) embeddings of the CM type. For this formula see [GL, Data.lean, l. 74 and BorderedDeterminant.lean, l. 768]. The pairing matrices used in \(I(\gamma)\) and \(I'(\gamma)\) are those of \(\gamma\) and \(\gamma^{-1}\) read in the finite adeles [GL, Terms.lean, l. 450]. Thus \(\operatorname{cal}(\gamma)\) is independent of \(c,c'\).

The tail scale is \(\mathrm{ts}:=b^{kf/4}\) and the pair scale \(\mathrm{pc}:=\#\bar R_0\cdot n_{\mathrm{cl}}/N^{kf}\), with \(n_{\mathrm{cl}}\) the number of classes. The cell moment \(D_{\mathrm{cell}}(\gamma)\) is \(D_{\mathrm{main}}\) if \(\operatorname{cr}(\gamma)=\varrho+1\) and \(D_{\mathrm{id}}/\mathrm{ts}^{16}\) otherwise, and the size of \(\gamma\) is \(\operatorname{sz}(\gamma):=\mathrm{ts}^2\bigl(D_{\mathrm{cell}}(\gamma)/(\mathrm{pc}\cdot\operatorname{cal}(\gamma)^k)\bigr)^{1/2}\).

(size). For a stable \(\mathfrak S\subseteq\Gamma^*\), all classes \(c,c'\) and all \(s\in\bar G\), \[\lVert\mathrm{Amp}^\flat(\mathfrak S;c,s,c')\rVert\le\nu\sum_{\gamma\in\mathrm{Rep}(\mathfrak S;c,s,c')}\operatorname{sz}(\gamma),\] a sum of nonnegative terms, possibly infinite.

For \(x_1,\dots,x_i,y_1,\dots,y_i\in{\mathbb{C}}^{n'}\), \[\lvert\det(\langle x_a,y_b\rangle)\rvert^2\le\det(\langle x_a,x_b\rangle)\det(\langle y_a,y_b\rangle).\] If all \(\langle x_a,y_b\rangle\) lie in \(M'{\mathbb{Z}}[\mathrm{i}]\) for an integer \(M'\ge1\) and the determinant is not \(0\), the product of the two Gram determinants is at least \(M'^{2i}\).

Let \(M'\ge1\) be an integer, \(\zeta_1\in\mathbb Q(\mathrm{i})\), \(\zeta_1\bar\zeta_1=1\), \(\zeta_1\ne1\), and let \(D'\ge1\) be an integer with \(D'(1-\zeta_1)\in M'{\mathbb{Z}}[\mathrm{i}]\). Then \(D'\ge M'/2\). For \(\zeta_1=(-12+5\mathrm{i})/13\), \(M'=5\), \(D'=13\): \(13(1-\zeta_1)=5(5-\mathrm{i})\), \(\lvert5-\mathrm{i}\rvert^2=26\), and \(\lvert1-\zeta_1\rvert\approx1.961\le2\).

\(g_1+g_2\sqrt5=2889+1292\sqrt5\); \(\gamma\) is an isometry of \(h\) and \(\gamma\equiv-1\bmod17\); modulo each of the primes \(4\pm\mathrm{i}\) above \(17\) it fixes the line of \(e_2\). The determinant \(\det(e_2,\gamma e_2)=-6460\) lies in both primes; its norm \(6460^2=289\cdot144400\) is divisible by \(17\cdot17\), while \(6460\equiv102\bmod289\).

Let \(\gamma,\gamma'\) lie over one block \((c,s,c')\), and let \(\mathrm{Lat}_c\) be the image under \(h_c\) of the lattice spanned by the lattice basis. The common link \(X_0(\gamma,\gamma')\subseteq X_0\) is the space of the \(x\in X_0\) for which some \(y\in X_0\) has \((x,y)\in\operatorname{lk}\gamma\cap\operatorname{lk}\gamma'\). Lattices are taken in the finite adelic points \(V(\mathbb A_{E,f})\) of \(E\)-spaces \(V\), and products in the lattice coordinates of \(c\). The term lattice \(L_\gamma\) is the set of \(x\in\mathrm{Lat}_c\cap X_0(\mathbb A_{E,f})\) whose pairings with the image of the Bessel tuple under \(\tilde\gamma\) are \(M\) times the products of some vector of \(\mathrm{Lat}_c\cap(Ev_1+\dots+Ev_\varrho)(\mathbb A_{E,f})\) with that image. The common lattice is \(L_{\gamma\gamma'}:=X_0(\gamma,\gamma')(\mathbb A_{E,f})\cap L_\gamma\cap L_{\gamma'}\). If it is spanned over \(\hat{\mathcal O}_E\) by the \(\delta_0:=\dim X_0(\gamma,\gamma')\) columns of a matrix \(\mathsf Q=\mathsf x\mathsf u\), where \(\mathsf x\) consists of \(\delta_0\) linearly independent vectors of \(X_0(\gamma,\gamma')\) and \(\mathsf u\) is an invertible \(\delta_0\times\delta_0\) matrix of finite adeles, its discriminant \(\operatorname{dsc}(\gamma,\gamma')\) is the square root of the inverse of the factor by which multiplication by \(\det(\mathsf Q^*\mathsf Q)\) scales Haar measure on the finite adeles, in orthonormal coordinates of \(X_0\); otherwise \(\operatorname{dsc}(\gamma,\gamma'):=0\). The corank is \(\operatorname{crk}(\gamma,\gamma'):=k-\dim X_0(\gamma,\gamma')\), and the link corank is \(\operatorname{lcr}(\gamma,\gamma'):=k+1-\dim(\operatorname{lk}\gamma\cap\operatorname{lk}\gamma')\), which vanishes if and only if \(\operatorname{lk}\gamma=\operatorname{lk}\gamma'\). Two terms are in the same link class if both discriminants are nonzero and their links are equal.

(congruence saving). Let \(\gamma,\gamma'\) have cell ranks and lie over one block \((c,s,c')\) with \(s\) agreeing; put \(i:=\operatorname{lcr}(\gamma,\gamma')\), \(\ell:=\operatorname{crk}(\gamma,\gamma')\). For every integer \(t_0\) with \(0\le t_0\le\operatorname{mt}(s)\), let \(X:=t_0\) if \(i=0\) and \(\operatorname{cr}(\gamma)=\varrho+1\), and \(X:=1\) otherwise. Then \((\operatorname{dsc}\cdot X)^2\le(2/M)^{2if}\operatorname{cal}(\gamma)\operatorname{cal}(\gamma')\). \(\ell\le i+(\operatorname{cr}(\gamma)-\varrho)_+\). If \(i=0\), then \(\operatorname{disc}(\gamma)=0\) if and only if \(\operatorname{disc}(\gamma')=0\). \(\operatorname{dsc}\ge1\); and if \((\gamma,\gamma')\) is a pair of near representatives, then \(\ell\le(\varrho+1)^3\) and \(\operatorname{dsc}\le b^{(\varrho+1)^3f}\).

(count). For every integer \(0\le\ell\le(\varrho+1)^3\), the sum of \(\operatorname{dsc}(\gamma,\gamma')^{-k}\) over all classes \(c,c'\) and the pairs of near representatives over \(c,c'\) of corank \(\ell\) with \(\operatorname{dsc}\le b^{(\varrho+1)^3f}\) is at most \(\mathrm{ts}^{\ell+2}\mathrm{pc}\).

Recall \(\operatorname{dsc}\ge1\) and \(\operatorname{cal}\ge1\). If \((\operatorname{dsc}\cdot\eta)^2\le\operatorname{cal}(\gamma)\operatorname{cal}(\gamma')\) and \(D_{\mathrm{cell}}(\gamma),D_{\mathrm{cell}}(\gamma')\le D\), then \(\operatorname{sz}(\gamma)\operatorname{sz}(\gamma')\le\mathrm{ts}^4D/(\mathrm{pc}\,\eta^k\operatorname{dsc}^k)\).

For the data and all classes \(c,c'\), let \(\mathcal Q_{c,c'}\) be a set of pairs of near representatives over \(c,c'\), and suppose that every \((\gamma,\gamma')\in\mathcal Q_{c,c'}\) admits \(\eta,D\) as in Problem 44.4.1 with \(\mathrm{ts}^{\ell+6}D/\eta^k\le B\). Then \(\sum_{c,c'}\sum_{(\gamma,\gamma')\in\mathcal Q_{c,c'}}\operatorname{sz}(\gamma)\operatorname{sz}(\gamma')\le\mathrm{ts}\cdot B\).

For the data, \(D_{\mathrm{cell}}\le D_{\mathrm{main}}\). If \(i\ge1\) and \(\ell\le i+1\), then \(\mathrm{ts}^{\ell+6}D_{\mathrm{main}}(M/2)^{-ifk}\le\mathrm{ts}^{-10}D_{\mathrm{id}}\). At \(i=1\), \(\ell=2\) the left side is at most \(b^{-35kf/9}D_{\mathrm{id}}\), the right side \(b^{-10kf/4}D_{\mathrm{id}}\).

If \(\operatorname{lk}\gamma=\operatorname{lk}\gamma'\) and \(\gamma,\gamma'\) are not in the same link class, then \(\operatorname{disc}\gamma=\operatorname{disc}\gamma'=0\), \(\ell=0\), and \(\eta=1\), \(D=D_{\mathrm{id}}/\mathrm{ts}^{16}\) give \(\mathrm{ts}^{\ell+6}D/\eta^k=\mathrm{ts}^{-10}D_{\mathrm{id}}\).

If \(\gamma,\gamma'\) are in the same link class over \((c,s,c')\) and \(1\le z_0\le\operatorname{mt}(s)\) is an integer, then \(\ell\le1\), and \(\eta=z_0\), \(D=D_{\mathrm{main}}\) satisfy Problem 44.4.1 with \(\mathrm{ts}\cdot\mathrm{ts}^{\ell+6}D_{\mathrm{main}}/z_0^k\le(b^{2f}/z_0)^kD_{\mathrm{main}}\).

(pairs). For the data: the sum of \(\operatorname{sz}(\gamma)\operatorname{sz}(\gamma')\) over all classes \(c,c'\) and all pairs of near representatives over \(c,c'\) that are not in the same link class is at most \(b^{-kf}D_{\mathrm{id}}\); for every integer \(z_0\ge1\), the same sum over the pairs in the same link class that lie over some \((c,s,c')\) with \(z_0\le\operatorname{mt}(s)\) is at most \((b^{2f}/z_0)^kD_{\mathrm{main}}\).

Four amplitudes \(2,-1,3,1\) with labels \(\Lambda,\Lambda,\Lambda',\varnothing\), where \(\Lambda\ne\Lambda'\) are links and \(\varnothing\) marks discriminant \(0\): the square of their sum is \(25\); the squares of the sums of the pieces \(\Lambda\), \(\Lambda'\) add to \(1+9=10\); the products \(\lvert a\rvert\lvert a'\rvert\) over the ordered pairs \((a,a')\) of amplitudes with different labels, or both labelled \(\varnothing\) (the amplitude \(1\) with itself), add to \(31\); and \(25\le10+31\).

For all \(c,s,c'\), \(\lVert\mathrm{Amp}^\flat(\Gamma^*;c,s,c')\rVert^2\) is at most \(\sum_\Lambda\lVert\mathrm{Amp}^\flat(\Gamma^*\cap\{\operatorname{disc}\ne0,\ \operatorname{lk}=\Lambda\};c,s,c')\rVert^2\) plus \(\nu^2\) times the sum of \(\operatorname{sz}(\gamma)\operatorname{sz}(\gamma')\) over the pairs in \(\mathrm{Rep}(\Gamma^*;c,s,c')^2\) that are not in the same link class.

For the data, let \(\mathcal B\subseteq\bar G\) and \(C_1\ge0\). If the link second moment of \(\{\gamma:\operatorname{disc}(\gamma)\ne0\}\) over \(\mathcal B\) is at most \(C_1\nu^2\), then the second moment of \(\Gamma^*\) over \(\mathcal B\) formed with the Bessel truncation is at most \(C_1+b^{-kf}D_{\mathrm{id}}\).

For the data, let \(z_0\ge1\) be an integer and \(\mathcal B\subseteq\bar G\) with \(z_0\le\operatorname{mt}(s)\) for every \(s\in\mathcal B\). Then the link second moment of \(\{\gamma:\operatorname{disc}(\gamma)\ne0\}\) over \(\mathcal B\) is at most \((b^{2f}/z_0)^kD_{\mathrm{main}}\,\nu^2\), which is Theorem 43.3.1 for the data.

(the tail). For every set \(\mathfrak S\) of terms and every \(\mathcal B\subseteq\bar G\), the second moment over \(\mathcal B\) of the differences \(\mathrm{Amp}(\mathfrak S;c,s,c')-\mathrm{Amp}^\flat(\mathfrak S;c,s,c')\) is at most \(b^{-40}D_{\mathrm{id}}\).

For the data, let \(\mathcal B\) avoid the scalar cosets and \(C_0\ge0\), and let the link second moment of \(\{\gamma:\operatorname{disc}(\gamma)\ne0\}\) over \(\mathcal B\) be at most \(C_0\nu^2\). Then the second moment of \(U(Y_0)(F)\smallsetminus R(F)\) over \(\mathcal B\) has square root at most \(\sqrt{C_0+b^{-kf}D_{\mathrm{id}}}+b^{-20}\sqrt{D_{\mathrm{id}}}\le\sqrt{C_0}+b^{-15}\sqrt{D_{\mathrm{id}}}\). The bound by \(\sqrt{C_0}+b^{-15}\sqrt{D_{\mathrm{id}}}\) is Theorem 43.3.2 for the data.
The open cell: Siegel’s formula and Poisson summation
§45.1. Head, last entry and residual isometry
§45.3. Poisson summation, one entry at a time

Let \(\omega\) be a residual isometry, and write \(\omega z=y+c_\omega z\) with \(y\in X\), \(c_\omega\in E\). Then \(\lvert h(z,\omega z)\rvert^2=N^2\lvert c_\omega\rvert^2\) and \[N\,h(y,y)=\lvert h(z,\omega z)\rvert^2-N^2 .\] Hence \(\lvert\tau h(z,\omega z)\rvert\ge N\) at every infinite place \(\tau\), with strict inequality at every \(\tau\) if \(y\ne0\) and equality at every \(\tau\) if \(y=0\).

Let \(\gamma\in U(Y_0)(F)\) have \(\langle\gamma\rangle_j\ne0\) for \(1\le j\le\varrho\). Define the head of \(\gamma\) by \(\operatorname{hd}(\gamma):=\bigl(\langle\gamma\rangle_{a+1}/\langle\gamma\rangle_a\bigr)_{0\le a<\varrho}\in(E^\times)^\varrho\). If also \(\langle\gamma\rangle_{\varrho+1}\ne0\), define the last entry of \(\gamma\) by \(\operatorname{le}(\gamma):=\langle\gamma\rangle_{\varrho+1}/\langle\gamma\rangle_\varrho\). A residual isometry of the last floor is a residual isometry of \(Y_0\).

For odd \(p\), the number of \(x\in(\mathbb{Z}/p)^6\) with \(\sum_ix_i^2=1\) is \(p^5-\chi_{-4}(p)p^2\), and the same holds with \(1\) replaced by any \(j\) prime to \(p\): by machine \(252\), \(3100\), \(16856\) for \(p=3,5,7\). For right-hand side \(1\), by machine there are \(61236=3^5\cdot252\) solutions modulo \(9\), and \(3\cdot2^{5e}/4\) solutions modulo \(2^e\) for \(e=2,3\) (\(768\), \(24576\)). For \(e\ge3\) the count modulo \(2^{e+1}\) is \(2^5\) times the count modulo \(2^e\). Hence \(\alpha_p(1)=1-\chi_{-4}(p)p^{-3}\) for odd \(p\), and \(\alpha_2(1)=3/4\).

Let \(q\) be a prime power. The form \(\sum_{i\le n}x_i^{q+1}\) on \(\mathbb F_{q^2}^n\) has \((q^n-(-1)^n)(q^{n-1}-(-1)^{n-1})\) nonzero isotropic vectors: \(9\), \(27\), \(135\) for \(q=2\) and \(n=2,3,4\). Divided by \(q^{2n-1}\) this is \((1-(-1)^nq^{-n})(1+(-1)^nq^{1-n})\).

With \(L(3,\chi_{-4})=\pi^3/32\): \(\frac{\pi^3}2\cdot\frac34\cdot\prod_{p\text{ odd}}\bigl(1-\chi_{-4}(p)p^{-3}\bigr)=12=r_{I_3}(1)\). For \(j=5\) the factor at \(5\) is \(\alpha_5(5)=3224/3125\), the factor at infinity is \(\alpha_\infty(5)=25\pi^3/2\), the other factors are those of \(j=1\), and the product is \(312=r_{I_3}(5)\).

(Siegel’s formula for one vector). Let \(E\) be a CM field with Weil data, \(k\ge3\), \(K'\) an open subgroup of the stabilizer of \(\hat{\mathcal O}_E^k\) in the finite adelic unitary group of \(y^*y\), \(\phi\ge0\) a locally constant, compactly supported, \(K'\)-invariant function on \(\mathbb{A}_{E,f}^k\), and \(\mathfrak n\in E\) with \(\bar{\mathfrak n}=\mathfrak n\) and \(\tau\mathfrak n>0\) at every infinite place. Then each sum \(\sum_{y\in E^k,\,y^*y=\mathfrak n}\phi(g^{-1}y)\) converges, and \[\begin{multline*} \sum_{[g]}\frac{1}{\#\mathrm{Aut}(g)}\sum_{\substack{y\in E^k\\ y^*y=\mathfrak n}}\phi(g^{-1}y)\\ =\Bigl(\sum_{[g]}\frac{1}{\#\mathrm{Aut}(g)}\Bigr)\lvert d_E\rvert^{1/4}\prod_\tau\frac{\pi^k(\tau\mathfrak n)^{k-1}}{(k-1)!} \int\!\!\int\phi(u)\,\psi_f\bigl(\tfrac12\zeta(u^*u-\mathfrak n)\bigr)\,du\,d\zeta , \end{multline*}\] where \([g]\) runs over the classes of level \(K'\), \(u\) over \(\mathbb{A}_{E,f}^k\) with \(\hat{\mathcal O}_E\) of volume \(\operatorname{vol}(\hat{\mathcal O}_E)\) in each coordinate, and \(\zeta\) over the self-adjoint finite adeles, with Haar measure giving the self-adjoint part of the finite adelic codifferent of \(E/\mathbb{Q}\) volume \(1\).
On \(\mathbb{Z}/5\), \(\mathfrak f(j)=2+\cos(2\pi j/5)\) has \(\hat{\mathfrak f}=(2,\tfrac12,0,0,\tfrac12)\). So \(\mathfrak f(0)=3\), while the zero frequency alone gives \(2\).

Let \(\mathfrak f\) be a function on a finite abelian group \(\mathcal G\), and \(\hat{\mathfrak f}(\psi'):=(\#\mathcal G)^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal G}\mathfrak f(j)\overline{\psi'(j)}\) for the characters \(\psi'\) of \(\mathcal G\). Then \(\lvert\mathfrak f(j)\rvert\le\sum_{\psi'}\lvert\hat{\mathfrak f}(\psi')\rvert\) for every \(j\), and \(\hat{\mathfrak f}(\psi_0)\) is the mean of \(\mathfrak f\), for the trivial character \(\psi_0\). If \(\mathfrak f\) is real and \(\sum_{\psi'\ne\psi_0}\lvert\hat{\mathfrak f}(\psi')\rvert\le c\), then \(\mathfrak f(j)\le\hat{\mathfrak f}(\psi_0)+c\).

Let \(\mathfrak A_l:=\bigl(\mathrm e(ljj'/3)\bigr)_{j,j'\in\mathbb{Z}/3}\). Then \(\mathfrak A_1\mathfrak A_1^*=3\cdot1\), and \(\mathfrak A_0\mathfrak A_0^*\) is the matrix with all entries \(3\). The squared operator norms of \(\mathfrak A_1\) and \(\mathfrak A_0\) are \(3\) and \(9\), respectively. For each integer \(k\ge1\), the squared operator norms of \(\mathfrak A_1^{\otimes k}\) and \(\mathfrak A_0^{\otimes k}\) are \(3^k\) and \(9^k\), respectively.
The entrywise product of two positive semidefinite matrices of the same size is positive semidefinite.

Let \(\pi\) be an irreducible unitary representation of a unimodular group \(\mathcal G'\) (whose left Haar measure is also right invariant) with square-integrable matrix coefficients and formal degree \(d_\pi\), so that \(\int_{\mathcal G'}\langle\pi(g)u_1,u_3\rangle\overline{\langle\pi(g)u_2,u_4\rangle}\,dg=d_\pi^{-1}\langle u_1,u_2\rangle\overline{\langle u_3,u_4\rangle}\). For every vector \(u\) with \(\lVert u\rVert^2=D'\), \[\int_{\mathcal G'}\lvert\langle\pi(g)u,u\rangle\rvert^2\,dg=\frac{D'^2}{d_\pi} .\] For the representation of Problem 10.5.5 and \(D'=1\), this is the reciprocal of the formal degree found there.

(one-sided Poisson summation). Let \(E\) be a totally complex number field with chosen complex embeddings, \(\psi\) the standard character of \(\mathbb{A}_E/E\), and \(du\) the Haar measure on \(\mathbb{A}_E\) for which \(E\) has covolume \(1\). Let \(\mathfrak f\colon\mathbb{A}_E\to\mathbb{R}\) be nonnegative and integrable, and lower semicontinuous at each point of a finite set \(\mathcal{Z}\subset E\), and put \(\hat{\mathfrak f}(l):=\int\mathfrak f(u)\psi(-lu)\,du\). If \(\sum_{l\in\mathcal{Z}'}\lvert\hat{\mathfrak f}(l)\rvert\le c_{\mathfrak f}\) for every finite \(\mathcal{Z}'\subset E\), then \(\sum_{u\in\mathcal{Z}}\mathfrak f(u)\le c_{\mathfrak f}\).

(the sieve). For the data, fix \(\mathcal{D}\) and the vectors of Theorem 45.3.3. Use the product sieve system of Section 46.4 for this fixer. Use the prefix weights of that section. Complete each rational tuple with entries \(1\), then read it at the finite places of the sieve and in the scaled Bessel tuple at each infinite place, as in Definition 46.2.2. There are real numbers \(\Sigma_0,\dots,\Sigma_{\varrho+1}\), the real parts of the sums of the form over all pairs of length-\(i\) heads in \(\mathcal E^i\) whose last entries agree (for \(i=0\), the real part of the form at the empty pair), and \(\lambda_0,\dots,\lambda_\varrho\ge0\), the sums of the weights of the heads of length \(i\) with entries in \(\mathcal E\). They satisfy, for \(0\le i\le\varrho\), \[\Sigma_0\le c_{\mathrm{bot}},\qquad \Sigma_{i+1}\le c_i\bigl(\Sigma_i+2c_{\mathrm{fr}}\lambda_i^2\bigr),\qquad \lambda_i^2\le c_{\mathrm{wt}}\prod_{i'<i}c_{i'} ,\] and for every \(U\subseteq\mathcal E\), \(\Sigma_{\varrho+1}\) bounds the real part of the sum of the top form over all \(t\in U\) and all ordered pairs of heads in \(\mathcal E^\varrho\) completed by \(t\). Here \(c_i>0\) is the constant of Poisson summation in the entry \(i\): \(\operatorname{vol}(\hat{\mathcal O}_E)\) divided by the Jacobian, at the infinite places, of the rescaling that the proof applies to that entry. Further \(c_{\mathrm{bot}}=\prod_\tau\bigl((1+b^{-10})/d_\tau\bigr)\cdot(1+b^{-6})\,b^{-6k\#\mathcal{D}}\), \(c_{\mathrm{fr}}=b^{2002(\varrho+1)^9f}c_{\mathrm{dec}}\), and \(c_{\mathrm{wt}}=b^{400(\varrho+1)^9f}\). Here \(c_{\mathrm{dec}}>0\) is the decay constant of the proof.

For the data, let \(\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathcal{M}_0\) be a set of chosen places above \(p_0\), and for each \(w\in\mathcal{D}\) choose \(w\) or \(\bar w\) and a nonzero vector in the span of the Bessel tuple modulo it, as in Definition 43.2.7; let the fixer of \(\mathcal{D}\) be the fixer of these vectors. Let a finite group \(G_0\) act on a finite set \(\mathcal X\), let \(\mathrm{Cut} \subset \mathcal X\) meet every orbit, and put \(\mathrm{mult}(y) := \#\{\gamma \in G_0 : \gamma^{-1}y \in \mathrm{Cut}\}\). Then for every function \(f \colon \mathcal X \to \mathbb{C}\), \[\sum_{y \in \mathcal X} f(y) = \sum_{\gamma \in G_0}\, \sum_{c \in \mathrm{Cut}} \frac{f(\gamma c)}{\mathrm{mult}(\gamma c)} .\] If \(f\) is \(G_0\)-invariant, the right side is \(\lvert G_0\rvert \sum_{c \in \mathrm{Cut}} f(c)/\mathrm{mult}(c)\); if \(\mathrm{Cut}\) has exactly one point in each orbit, then \(\mathrm{mult}(c) = \lvert\operatorname{Stab}_{G_0}(c)\rvert\) for \(c \in \mathrm{Cut}\). For \(G_0 = (\mathbb{Z}/5)^\times\) acting on \(\mathcal X = \mathbb{Z}/5\) by multiplication, \(\mathrm{Cut} = \{0,1,2\}\) and \(f = 1\), the multiplicities are \(4, 2, 2\) and both sides equal \(5\).

A space with a string for \(N\) is a hermitian space \(V\) over \(E\) with a basis consisting of an orthonormal basis of a subspace \(X\) and vectors \(f_0,\dots,f_{s-1}\) orthogonal to \(X\), and with a constant \(c_V\in F^\times\), such that \(f_i\) pairs only with \(f_{s-1-i}\), to \(1\), or to \(-N\) if \(i=s-1-i\). We write \(J_V\) for the Gram matrix. \(X\) is the definite part, \(f_0,\dots,f_{s-1}\) is the string, and \(\operatorname{len}V:=s\) is its length.

The grade of a vector of the basis of \(X\) is \(0\), and that of \(f_i\) is \(s-1-2i\). Let \(V'\) be a second space with a string, and let \(d\) be integer weights on the basis of \(V'\). For basis vectors \(e\) of \(V\) and \(e'\) of \(V'\), the entry of a map \(w\colon V\to V'\) in the row of \(e'\) and the column of \(e\) has degree \(d(e')-\operatorname{grade}(e)\), and \(w\) has degree \(\ge i\) if all its entries of degree \(<i\) vanish. For maps \(V\to V\) the weights are the grades.

Let \(\operatorname{len}V'=\operatorname{len}V-1\), or \(\operatorname{len}V=\operatorname{len}V'=0\). The string map \(\mathrm{st}\colon V\to V'\) kills the definite part and sends \(f_i\) to \(f'_i\) times a scalar, and to \(0\) if \(V'\) has no vector \(f'_i\). If \(\operatorname{len}V\) is odd, the scalar is \(1,\ -Nc_V,\ c_V\) for \(f_i\) of positive, zero, negative grade; if \(\operatorname{len}V\) is even, it is \(c_V,\ 1\) for positive, negative grade. For a map \(w\colon V\to V'\) put \(w^*:=J_V^{-1}\bar w^{t}J_{V'}\).

The unitary upper unitriangular matrices for \(J_V\) are the \(27\) matrices \(u=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&a&b\\0&1&\bar a\\0&0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) with \(b+\bar b=a\bar a\). They form \(\mathcal{U}\), and \(u-1\) has degree \(\ge2\) for each of them.
\(\operatorname{tr}(\mathrm{st}^*\mathrm{st}\,u)=a-\bar a\), and for \(w=(v,0,0)\) with first column \(v\in\mathbb{F}_9^2\), \(\operatorname{tr}(w^*wu)=(\bar v^{t}J_{V'}v)\,b\).

Let \(d\) be weights on the basis of \(V'\). A rational map \(w\colon V\to V'\) survives for \(d\) if \[\psi_E\bigl(\tfrac12j_E\operatorname{tr}(\mathrm{st}^*\mathrm{st}\,u)\bigr)=\psi_E\bigl(\tfrac12j_E\operatorname{tr}(w^*w\,u)\bigr)\] for every \(u\in\mathcal{U}(\mathbb{A}_F)\) such that \(u-1\) has degree \(\ge2\) and \(w(u-1)\) has degree \(\ge1\) for the weights \(d\). A map \(w\) agrees with \(\mathrm{st}\) if \(w\) and \(\mathrm{st}\) have the same entry in the row of \(e'\) and the column of \(e\) whenever \(\operatorname{grade}(e)>0\) and \(\operatorname{grade}(e')<\operatorname{grade}(e)\).
In the hook, take the weights \((0,0)\). The classes are represented by the \(81\) maps \(w=(v,0,0)\), and exactly \(32\) of them survive: the \(v\ne0\) with \(\bar v^{t}J_{V'}v=0\).

The unitary group \(U(V')(\mathbb{F}_3)=\{g\in\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_9):\bar g^{t}J_{V'}g=J_{V'}\}\) has \(96\) elements, and their first columns are the \(32\) surviving vectors of Problem 53.3.1. The stabilizer of \((1,0)^{t}\) has order \(3\) and is the Bessel subgroup \(R'\) of \(V'\).

Take the weights \((1,-1)\), the grades of \(V'\). The classes that agree with \(\mathrm{st}\) are represented by the nine maps \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0&0\\0&c&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), \(c\in\mathbb{F}_9\), and exactly \(c=-1\) survives: the class of \(\mathrm{st}\).

The part of grade zero of \(Y_{m-2}^- \oplus Y_m\), which is the whole space, is \(X_{m-2}^- \oplus X_m\) with \(X_m = Y_m \perp E\,f_{\mathrm{mid}}/\pi_N\), and \(h \in U(Y_m)\) acts on \(X_m\) as \(\operatorname{diag}(h, 1)\).

In the last pair the only map of positive degree between any two of \(V, V', V''\) is zero; \(R_{m-2} = U(X_{m-2})\) and \(R_{m-1} = U(Y_{m-1})\); the string maps \(\mathrm{st}_{m-1}\), \(\mathrm{st}_m\) vanish; and \(\mathrm{CT}_{\mathrm{st}_{m-1}}\phi = \theta(\phi)\), \(\mathrm{CT}_{\mathrm{st}_m}\phi' = \theta(\phi')\) for all data.

In the last pair, for all data \(\phi, \phi'\), \(\gamma \in U(X_{m-2})(\mathbb{A})\), \(\gamma' \in U(Y_{m-1})(\mathbb{A})\) and \(h \in U(Y_m)(\mathbb{A})\), \[\mathrm{CT}_{\mathrm{st}_{m-1}}\bigl(\omega(\gamma, \gamma')\phi\bigr)\,\mathrm{CT}_{\mathrm{st}_m}\bigl(\omega'(\gamma', h)\phi'\bigr) = z_\theta^{-1}\,\theta\Bigl(\omega^\triangle\bigl(\gamma, \gamma', \operatorname{diag}(h, 1)\bigr)\,\mathrm{zt}(\phi \boxtimes \phi')\Bigr) .\]

Let \(V, V', V''\) be spaces with strings for the same \(N\), of lengths \(s+1, s, \max(s-1, 0)\) \((s \ge 0)\), with string maps \(\mathrm{st}_1 \colon V \to V'\) and \(\mathrm{st}_2 \colon V' \to V''\). Define the stacked string map by \(A := \binom{\mathrm{st}_1^*}{\mathrm{st}_2} \colon V' \to V^- \oplus V''\).

Let \(s \ge 1\) and \(c_V = c_{V'}\). Then \(\mathrm{st}_1\mathrm{st}_1^* = \mathrm{st}_2^*\mathrm{st}_2\); this map kills the definite part and \(f'_{s-1}\) and sends \(f'_q\) to a multiple of \(f'_{q+1}\) for \(q < s - 1\). Also \(A^*A = -\mathrm{st}_1\mathrm{st}_1^* + \mathrm{st}_2^*\mathrm{st}_2 = 0\).

Under the hypotheses of Problem 54.3.4, \((An')^*(An) = 0\) and \(\mathrm{Heis}(An)\mathrm{Heis}(An') = \mathrm{Heis}(A(n + n'))\) on \(\operatorname{Hom}(V', V^- \oplus V'')\), for all adelic endomorphisms \(n, n'\) of \(V'\).

For data \(\phi^\triangle\) on \(\operatorname{Hom}(V',V^-\oplus V'')\) let \(\mathrm{zt}_{>0}(\phi^\triangle)\) average \(\theta(\mathrm{Heis}(b)\phi^\triangle)\) over the positive-degree adelic maps in this space modulo rational maps, using the grades on both summands. For adelic \(w:V\to V'\), \(w':V'\to V''\) and all data, \[\mathrm{CT}_w \phi \cdot \mathrm{CT}_{w'} \phi' = z_\theta^{-1}\,\mathrm{zt}_{>0}\bigl(\mathrm{Heis}(w)\phi \boxtimes \mathrm{Heis}(w')\phi'\bigr) .\]
If \(\operatorname{len}V\) is odd, all grades of \(V\) are even, and \(n - 1\) has degree \(\ge 2\) for every \(n \in \mathcal{U}(\mathbb{A})\).

For norms \(5\), \(-5\), the basis \(\tfrac1{10}(f_{\mathrm{mid}}- f_{\mathrm{mid}}')\), \(f_{\mathrm{mid}}+ f_{\mathrm{mid}}'\) of the plane they span has Gram matrix \(\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} 0&1\\ 1&0 \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\); in general so has \((f_{\mathrm{mid}}- f_{\mathrm{mid}}')/2N\), \(f_{\mathrm{mid}}+ f_{\mathrm{mid}}'\).

Let \(\operatorname{len}Y_j\) be odd and \(\mathcal{W}\) be equivariant on \(R_j(\mathbb{A})\) with \(\mathcal{W}(\gamma) = \operatorname{coeff}_l\psi(\gamma)\) for all \(\gamma \in U(X_j)(\mathbb{A})\). Then \(\mathcal{W}= \mathcal{W}_{l,\psi}\).

For pair \(i\), \(0\le i\le\varrho\), define the evaluated pair datum to be the pair tensor \[\begin{gather*} \phi^{\mathrm{ev}}_i(\xi, y) := \boxtimes^{-1}\,\mathrm{zt}_f\,\mathrm{Heis}_f(A_f)\bigl(\mathbf 1_{2i+1}(\xi)^y \boxtimes \mathbf 1_{2i+2}(\xi)^y\bigr), \\ \text{where } \mathbf 1_j(\xi)^y := \omega_j(y_{j-1}, y_j)\,\mathbf 1_j(\xi) . \end{gather*}\]

Suppose \(\mathcal{W}^{\mathrm{tr}}_{2i}=\mathcal{W}_{l,\psi}\), with \(\psi\) a form on \(X_{2i}\). Use \(l''\) from (E) for \(l\) and \(\mathbf u=(c_Rc_{R'}/z_\theta)\mathbf u_i\). For all \(h\in U(X''_0)(\mathbb{A})\), \[\mathcal{W}_{2i+2}\bigl(h\,(g_{2i+2}, y_{2i+2})\bigr) = \operatorname{coeff}_{l''}\Bigl(\sum\Theta^X_{\xi,2i+2}(v')\,\Theta^X_{\xi,2i+1}(v)\,\psi\Bigr)(\bar h)\] if \(\phi^{\mathrm{ev}}_i(\xi, y) = \sum v \otimes v'\), and \(l''\) does not depend on \(\xi\), \(\psi\) or the finite points.

(two lifts at a time). Fix \(\lambda\), archimedean points \(g_k\) of \(U(Y_k)\) \((k \ge 0)\) and \(0 \le i \le \varrho\). There is a linear form \(l\) on the values of forms on \(X_{2i+2}\) such that for every tame character \(\xi\), every \(\varphi \in S\), all finite points \(y_k \in U(Y_k)(\mathbb{A}_f)\), and every \(h\) in \(U(X_{2i+2})(\mathbb{A})\) if \(i < \varrho\), in \(U(Y_m)(\mathbb{A})\) if \(i = \varrho\), \[\mathcal{W}_{2i+2}\bigl(h\,(g_{2i+2}, y_{2i+2})\bigr) = \operatorname{coeff}_l\Bigl(\Theta^X_\xi\bigl(\phi^{\mathrm{ev}}_i(\xi, y) \otimes \dots \otimes \phi^{\mathrm{ev}}_0(\xi, y)\bigr)\varphi\Bigr)(\bar h) .\] Here \(h\) acts through the definite part of \(Y_{2i+2}\), with \(\bar h=h\) for \(i<\varrho\) and \(\bar h=\operatorname{diag}(h,1)\in U(X_m)(\mathbb{A})\) for \(i=\varrho\).
Lattices, cuts and the ramified forms

Let \(y\) and \(z'\) be functions on \([U(Y_0)]\), fixed by right translation by \(K_M\) and by \(K^{Y}_{0}(\xi)\) respectively, with \(y z'\) integrable. Then \[\int_{[U(Y_0)]} y(h)\sum_{c\in K_M/K^{Y}_{0}(\xi)} z'(hc)\,dh=[K_M:K^{Y}_{0}(\xi)]\int_{[U(Y_0)]}y\,z' .\] Hence, for every tame \(\xi\), every \(\varphi\in S\) and every form \(z\) on \(Y_1\) as in Problem 54.2.3, \[\int_{[U(Y_1)]} z\;\Theta_{\xi,1}\mathcal{P}_{g,\lambda}\varphi=[K^{Y\circ}_{0}:K_M]\sum_{c\in K_M/K^{Y}_{0}(\xi)}\ \int_{R_1(F)\backslash U(Y_1)(\mathbb{A})}\mathcal{W}_1\,z ,\] where the summand uses \((g,\tilde c)\) in outer slot \(0\), with \(\tilde c\in K_M\) any representative of \(c\), and the identity in every other slot.

Let \(B_j\) be the finite component of the adelic frame of Section 37.3. The lattice \(\Lambda(x)\) of \(x\in U(Y_j)(\mathbb{A}_f)\) consists of the finite adelic vectors whose coordinates in the frame \(B_jx\) are integral. In rational coordinates, \(\Lambda(x)=(B_jxB_j^{-1})\Lambda(1)\). Define the string parts of \(\Lambda(x)\) by \(\Lambda^-(x):=\Lambda(x)\cap X_j^\perp\) and \(\Lambda^+(x):=\operatorname{pr}\Lambda(x)\), where \(\operatorname{pr}\) is the orthogonal projection to \(X_j^\perp\). We write \(\Lambda^\pm_j\) when the stage must be named.
A lattice is graded if it contains the part of each grade of each of its vectors.

Over a DVR, or a product of two exchanged by the involution, let \(\Lambda\) be a lattice, self-dual for a nondegenerate hermitian form, in a space \(W\perp W'\). Then the dual of \(\Lambda\cap W\) in \(W\) is the projection of \(\Lambda\) to \(W\). Hence, for \(x,x'\in U(Y_j)(\mathbb{A}_f)\) and a finite idele \(\varpi\), \(\varpi\Lambda^-(x)\subseteq\Lambda^-(x')\) implies \(\bar\varpi\Lambda^+(x')\subseteq\Lambda^+(x)\).
A function on \(\mathbb{Z}/25\) invariant under translation by \(5\mathbb{Z}/25\) has Fourier transform supported on \(5\mathbb{Z}/25\).

Let \(\varpi_\xi\) and \(\varpi_M\) be the generator ideles fixed in the proof for the ideals \((\pi_M)\prod_{w\in Q_\xi}w\) and \((\pi_M)\); each has component \(1\) away from the places dividing its ideal. Define the idele of the modulus by \(\mathfrak{u}:=\varpi_\xi/\varpi_M\). It is a uniformizer at every \(w\in Q_\xi\) and a unit at every other finite place.

Use the string matrices \(J_3=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&0&1\\0&-5&0\\1&0&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), \(J_2=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) and \(\mathrm{st}_1=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0&0\\0&-5&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) of Chapter 54 (\(N=5\), string constant \(1\)), and let \(\hat{\mathcal{O}}\) be the integral finite adeles of \(\mathbb{Q}(\mathrm{i})\). On the first string let \(L^-=\hat{\mathcal{O}}^3\) and \(L^+=\operatorname{diag}(1,\tfrac15,1)\hat{\mathcal{O}}^3\), on the second \(L'=\hat{\mathcal{O}}^2\). Then \(L^-\) and \(L^+\) are dual for \(J_3\), \(L'\) is self-dual for \(J_2\), and \(\mathrm{st}_1L^+=L'\).

A point \(x\in U(Y_j)(\mathbb{A}_f)\) has the lattice bounds at stage \(j\) if \(\bar{\mathfrak{u}}^{\,j}\Lambda^-_j(1)\subseteq\Lambda^-_j(x)\) and \(\mathfrak{u}^{\,j}\Lambda^-_j(x)\subseteq\Lambda^-_j(1)\).

Let \(0\le j\le m-2\), and suppose \(\mathfrak{u}^{\,j}\Lambda^-_j(r_1x)\subseteq\Lambda^-_j(1)\) and \((\bar{\mathfrak{u}}/\mathfrak{a})\,\mathrm{st}_{j+1}\Lambda^+_j(r_1x)\subseteq\Lambda^-_{j+1}(r_2x')\). Then \(\bar{\mathfrak{u}}^{\,j+1}\Lambda^-_{j+1}(1)\subseteq\Lambda^-_{j+1}(r_2x')\).
\(\Lambda(x)\) is split at a finite place \(w\) if \(1_w\Lambda^+(x)\subseteq\Lambda^-(x)\), where \(1_w\) is the idempotent finite adele that is \(1\) at \(w\) and \(0\) elsewhere.

Let \(1\le j\le m-1\) and \(\bar{\mathfrak{u}}^{\,j}\Lambda^-_j(1)\subseteq\Lambda^-_j(x)\), but \(\mathfrak{u}^{\,j}\Lambda^-_j(x)\not\subseteq\Lambda^-_j(1)\). Then some \(\mathfrak{u}^{\,j}v\), \(v\in\Lambda^-_j(x)\), lies in \(\Lambda^+_j(1)\) but not in \(\Lambda^-_j(1)\). Moreover, the string of \(Y_j\) is odd, \(j\) is even, and \(\Lambda(x)\) is split at a place \(w\) dividing \(\pi_N\).

For \(z=\operatorname{diag}(2,1)\), the scaling of the definite coordinate by a generator of \((\mathbb{Z}/5)^\times\): \(B^{-1}zB=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2&0\\-1/5&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) is not integral, and \(D'^{-1}zD'=z\).

Suppose \(\omega^X(z_w,z_w)\) acts trivially on the data of every lift \(X_k\to X_{k+1}\), and \(\omega^X(1,z_w)\), acting on one factor alone, fixes a tensor \(v\) of data. Then the (partial) chain \(\Theta^X_\xi(v)\) satisfies \(\Theta^X_\xi(v)\,T_w=\Theta^X_\xi(v)\), and it vanishes on \(S_{\mathrm{ram}}\).

Let \(\varphi\in S_{\mathrm{ram}}\), \(2\le j\le m-1\) even, and \(\Lambda(x)\) split at some \(w\mid\pi_N\). Then \(\mathcal{W}_j(\gamma(g_\infty,x))=0\) for every \(\gamma\in R_j(\mathbb{A})\) and every archimedean point \(g_\infty\).

Let \(\varphi\in S_{\mathrm{ram}}\), \(y_0\in K_M\), \(1\le j\le m-1\), and \(\mathcal{W}_j(g_\infty,x)\ne0\). Then \(r_2x\) has the lattice bounds at stage \(j\) for every \(r_2\in R_j(\mathbb{A}_f)\) with \(\Lambda(r_2x)\) graded.

Let \(G_0=H=S_3\) act on \(H/H_0\), \(G_1=H_0:=\langle(1\,2)\rangle\), \(x=(1\,2\,3)\), \(\mathrm{Cut}:=\{h xH_0:h\in H_0\}\subset H/H_0\). Then \(\#\mathrm{Cut}=2\), the multiplicities of the three cosets are \(2,2,2\), and for \(f_1(hH_0):=h(3)\), \[\sum_{t\in H/H_0}f_1(t)=6=\sum_{rH_0\in H/H_0}\ \sum_{c\in\mathrm{Cut}}\frac{f_1(rc)}{\mathrm{mult}(rc)} .\]

\(\mathrm{Cut}_0(\xi)\) is the set of classes modulo \(K^{Y}_{0}(\xi)\) of the elements of \(K_M\), with \(\mathrm{mult}_0:=1\). For \(1\le j\le m-1\), let \(G_0=R_j(\mathbb{A}_f)\) and \(G_1=R_j(\mathbb{A}_f)\cap K^{Y\circ}_{j}\) act on \(U(Y_j)(\mathbb{A}_f)/K^{Y}_{j}(\xi)\); write \(\mathrm{mult}_j\) for the multiplicity above. A cut at stage \(j\) is a finite set \(\mathrm{Cut}_j(\xi)\) of classes such that: (a) it is \(G_1\)-stable; (b) its points are integral at every place not above a prime dividing \(\mathrm{Nm}\,Q_\xi\); (c) on it \(\mathrm{mult}_j\) divides a power of \(\mathrm{Nm}\,Q_\xi\); (d) \(\mathrm{mult}_j(x)\ne0\) whenever the \(G_0\)-orbit of \(x\) contains a point with graded lattice and the lattice bounds at stage \(j\). The proof fixes one cut at each stage.

Let \(C\) meet each \(G_0\)-orbit in at most one point, and \(\mathrm{Cut}=G_1\cdot C\). For \(c\in C\), \(\mathrm{mult}(c)=[\operatorname{Stab}_c:\operatorname{Stab}_c\cap G_1]\) with \(\operatorname{Stab}_c:=\operatorname{Stab}_{G_0}(c)\) (index \(0\) if infinite); and \(\mathrm{mult}(st)=\mathrm{mult}(t)\) for \(s\in G_0\).

(a) Let \(q,n\) be nonnegative integers. A finite group in which every element has order dividing \(q^n\) has order dividing a power of \(q\). (b) For \(u\equiv1\pmod p\) in \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z}_p)\) and \(x=\operatorname{diag}(p^{-2},1)\), \(xu^px^{-1}\) is integral; for \(p=3\), \(u=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}4&3\\3&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), \(xux^{-1}\) is not. (c) For the \(G_1\)-saturation of the classes chosen in the construction above, every \(c\) has \(\mathrm{mult}_j(c)\mid(\mathrm{Nm}\,Q_\xi)^n\) for some \(n\ge0\).

For \(0\le j<m\), if \(Q_\xi=\varnothing\), every finite point representing a class of \(\mathrm{Cut}_j(\xi)\) lies in \(K^{Y\circ}_{j}\), and \(\#\mathrm{Cut}_j(\xi)\le\#\mathrm{GL}_{r+jt}(\mathcal{O}_E/\pi_M)\le M^{f(r+jt)^2}\le M^{fn_m^2}\).

Let \(F_\infty\) be a function on \(U(Y_j)_\infty\). There is \(k(F_\infty)\in\mathbb{C}\) with the following property, for every level \(K'\), every finite \(G_1\)-stable set \(\mathrm{Cut}\) of classes modulo \(K'\), every complex function \(h_1\) on \(U(Y_j)(\mathbb{A}_f)/K'\) and every continuous left \(R_j(F)\)-invariant function \(f_1\) on \(U(Y_j)(\mathbb{A})\), integrable on \(R_j(F)\backslash U(Y_j)(\mathbb{A})\), with \(\mathrm{mult}(x_f)\ne0\) wherever \(f_1(x)\ne0\). If \(\int_{[R_j]}f_1(rx)\,dr=[K^{Y\circ}_{j}:K']\,F_\infty(x_\infty)\,h_1(x_fK')\) whenever \(x_fK'\in\mathrm{Cut}\), then \[\int_{R_j(F)\backslash U(Y_j)(\mathbb{A})}f_1=k(F_\infty)\sum_{c\in\mathrm{Cut}}\frac{h_1(c)}{\mathrm{mult}(c)} .\]

Let \(l\) be a linear form on the value space of the algebraic forms on \(X_m\) of the prescribed weight. There is \(c(l)\in\mathbb{C}\) with the following property, for every such form \(\psi\) and every \(h'\) with \(h'(g_\infty,x)=\langle v^+,\rho(g_\infty^{-1})P'(x)\rangle\) for an algebraic form \(P'\) on \(Y_m\) of the weight of the lower chain. Identify \(Y_m\) with the complement of the last basis vector of \(X_m\). If \(F'(k)\) is the coefficient of \(\psi\) at \(l\), evaluated at \(\operatorname{diag}(k,1)\), for every \(k\in U(Y_m)(\mathbb{A})\), then \[\int_{[U(Y_m)]}F'\,\overline{h'}=c(l)\int_{[U(Y_m)]}(\mathrm{res}\psi)\,\overline{h'} ,\] where \(v^+\) is the highest-weight vector, \(\rho\) the action on the value space, the product is conjugate-linear in the first variable, and on the right \(\mathrm{res}\psi\) is read in the same way.

Define the seesaw tensor of a tame character \(\xi\) by \[\mathrm{ss}_\xi:=\sum_{c_0\in\mathrm{Cut}_0(\xi),\dots,c_{m-1}\in\mathrm{Cut}_{m-1}(\xi)}\Bigl(\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}\frac1{\mathrm{mult}_j(c_j)}\Bigr)\,\bigl(\phi^{\mathrm{ev}}_\varrho(\xi,c)\otimes\dots\otimes\phi^{\mathrm{ev}}_0(\xi,c)\bigr),\] with \(c_m:=1\), in the order of Chapter 54; the evaluated data do not depend on the representatives of the classes.

Let \(\lambda\) be a linear form on the values of source forms and \(g\) a point of the archimedean unitary group of \(Y_0\). There is \(c'\in\mathbb{C}\), possibly zero, such that for every tame character \(\xi\) and every \(\varphi\in S_{\mathrm{ram}}\) \[\Theta_{\xi,m}\cdots\Theta_{\xi,1}\mathcal{P}_{g,\lambda}\varphi=c'\,\mathrm{res}\,\Theta^X_\xi(\mathrm{ss}_\xi)\varphi ,\] an equality of automorphic forms on \(Y_m\), with \(\mathrm{res}\) read in automorphic forms.
The seesaw tensor: translated vacua, gluing and the unit
§56.6. The unit and the seesaw identity

Let \((w_\gamma)_{\gamma\in\mathcal Z}\) be vectors of a complex vector space, \(\mathfrak d\ge1\) an integer and \(\mathfrak s\ge0\) real. A vector \(z\) is a combination of the \(w_\gamma\), \(\gamma\in\mathcal Z\), with denominator \(\mathfrak d\) and size \(\mathfrak s\) if \(z=\sum_{\gamma\in\mathcal Z}r_\gamma w_\gamma\) with finitely many nonzero \(r_\gamma\in\mathbb{C}\), \(\mathfrak d\,r_\gamma\in\mathcal{O}^{[q]}\) for every \(\gamma\) and, if \(Q_\xi=\varnothing\), \(\sum_\gamma\lvert\sigma(r_\gamma)\rvert\le\mathfrak s\) for every \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}\mathbb{C}\).

The point mass at \(\mathfrak i\) is \(\lvert \mathsf A_{\mathfrak m}\rvert^{-1}\sum_{\mathfrak b}\psi_{\mathfrak m}(-\mathfrak i\cdot\mathfrak b)\,\chi_{\mathfrak b}\). Hence \(\mathbf 1_j(\xi)=\lvert \mathsf A_{\mathfrak m}\rvert^{-1}\sum_{\mathfrak b}\psi_{\mathfrak m}(-\mathfrak i\cdot\mathfrak b)\,\mathrm{Heis}(t_{\mathfrak b})\mathrm{vac}\), and for every \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}\mathbb{C}\) the absolute values of the \(\sigma\)-conjugates of these coefficients sum to \(1\).

Each \(\bar\pi_Mt_{\mathfrak b}\) is integral away from \(q\), and \(\#(\mathcal{O}_E/\pi_M\mathcal{O}_E)^n\) divided by \(\lvert \mathsf A_{\mathfrak m}\rvert\) is \(q^{-n}\in\mathcal{O}^{[q]}\). So \(\mathbf 1_j(\xi)\) is a combination of the \(\mathrm{Heis}({\mathfrak{z}})\mathrm{vac}\), over the \({\mathfrak{z}}\) with \(\bar\pi_M{\mathfrak{z}}\) integral away from \(q\), with denominator \(\#(\mathcal{O}_E/\pi_M\mathcal{O}_E)^n\) and size \(1\).
Let \(h\in U(V)(\mathbb A_f)\). A vector \(f\) of the finite part with \(\mathrm{Heis}(h{\mathfrak{z}})f=f\) for all \({\mathfrak{z}}\in\Lambda\) is a multiple of \(\omega(h)\mathrm{vac}\).

Let \(h\in U(V)(\mathbb A_f)\) be integral away from \(q\), and let \(\bar\pi_M{\mathfrak{z}}_0\) be integral away from \(q\). Then \(\omega(h)\mathrm{Heis}({\mathfrak{z}}_0)\mathrm{vac}\) is a combination of the \(\mathrm{Heis}({\mathfrak{z}})\mathrm{vac}\), over the \({\mathfrak{z}}\) with \(\bar\pi_M{\mathfrak{z}}\) integral away from \(q\), with denominator \(1\) and size \(1\).

Let \(F\) be a nonarchimedean local field with integers \(\mathcal{O}_F\), \(W\) a finite-dimensional \(F\)-vector space with a nondegenerate symmetric or alternating bilinear form, \(L\subset W\) a lattice with \(L=\{x:\langle x,L\rangle\subseteq\mathcal{O}_F\}\), and \(I\subseteq W\) an isotropic subspace. Then the image of \(L\cap I^\perp\) in \(I^\perp/I\) is a lattice equal to its own dual.

Over a commutative ring with involution, let \(z\) be a column with \(z^*z=1\), \(\delta\) a scalar and \(\gamma:=1+(\delta-1)zz^*\). Then \(\gamma z=\delta z\), \(\gamma z'=z'\) when \(z^*z'=0\), and \(\gamma^*\gamma=1\) if and only if \(\delta\bar\delta=1\). Moreover \(e_P^*e_P=1\) and \(\pi_P\bar\pi_P=1\).

Define the neighbour lattice of pair \(i\) as the image of the standard lattice of \(\operatorname{Hom}(X_{2i+1},X_{2i}^-\oplus X_{2i+2})\) under the matrix acting on the target as \(\gamma_P:=1+(\pi_P-1)e_Pe_P^*\) at the places above \(N\), and at the other finite places as the identity for \(i<\varrho\); for \(i=\varrho\), at these places it scales the last row of \(X_{m}\) by \(\varpi_M/\bar\varpi_M\) and fixes the other rows, \(\varpi_M\) the generator idele of \((\pi_M)\) of Definition 55.2.6.

In this model \(e_P=\bigl((1,1),(0,1)\bigr)\), \(\pi_P=(5,\tfrac15)\), and the components of \(\gamma_P\) at \(w\) and \(\bar w\) are \(G=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}5&4\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) and \(G'=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1/5&0\\-4/5&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), with \(G^tG'=1\).

\(G\) is integral, and \(G'\mathbb{Z}_5^2+\mathbb{Z}_5^2=\mathbb{Z}_5^2+\mathbb{Z}_5\cdot\tfrac15(1,1)^t\); the five classes modulo \(\mathbb{Z}_5^2\) are those of \(\tfrac15(y,y)^t\), \(y=0,\dots,4\). The translation attached to \(y\) is \(-\tfrac15(y,y)^t\) at \(\bar w\), so one residue labels both rows.

Let \(\mathrm{sw}\) exchange the coordinates of \(\mathbb{Q}^2\). For \(v=(1,2)^t\) and \(v'=(3,-1)^t\), the sum of the matrices in the orbit of \(v{v'}^t\) under \(X\mapsto\mathrm{sw}\,X\,\mathrm{sw}^t\) is \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&5\\5&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) and is fixed by this action.

Let a group \(H\) act on finite sets \(\mathcal X_0,\dots,\mathcal X_{m-1}\) and linearly on a complex vector space; let \(\mathrm{mult}_j\colon\mathcal X_j\to\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\) be \(H\)-invariant and \(\mathcal E\) a function on \(\mathcal X_0\times\dots\times\mathcal X_{m-1}\) with \(\mathcal E(bc)=b\,\mathcal E(c)\) for \(b\in H\). Then \(\sum_c\prod_j\mathrm{mult}_j(c_j)^{-1}\mathcal E(c)\) is fixed by \(H\).

Substituting \(1,2,3\) for the three \(Y\)-dimensions and for the three \(X\)-ranks in \(\mathfrak e_i\) gives \(16\le4\cdot3^2\). For the ranks of the proof, \(\mathfrak e_i\le4n_m^2\), so \(\#(\mathcal{O}_E/\pi_M\mathcal{O}_E)^{\mathfrak e_i}\) divides \(c_{\mathrm{res}}^4\).

Let \(z\) be a combination of the \(w_\gamma\), \(\gamma\in\mathcal Z\), with denominator \(\mathfrak d\) and size \(\mathfrak s\), and let each \(w_\gamma\) be a combination of the \(w'_{\gamma'}\), \(\gamma'\in\mathcal Z'\), with denominator \(\mathfrak d'\) and size \(\mathfrak s'\). Then \(z\) is a combination of the \(w'_{\gamma'}\) with denominator \(\mathfrak d\mathfrak d'\) and size \(\mathfrak s\mathfrak s'\). If \(z_k\) is a combination of the \(w_{k,\gamma}\) with denominator \(\mathfrak d_k\) and size \(\mathfrak s_k\) \((k<l)\), then \(z_{l-1}\otimes\dots\otimes z_0\) is a combination of the \(w_{l-1,\gamma_{l-1}}\otimes\dots\otimes w_{0,\gamma_0}\) with denominator \(\prod_k\mathfrak d_k\) and size \(\prod_k\mathfrak s_k\).

Each \(\mathrm{mult}_j(c)^{-1}\), \(c\in\mathrm{Cut}_j(\xi)\), lies in \(\mathcal{O}^{[q]}\), and if \(Q_\xi=\varnothing\), then \(\sum_{c_0,\dots,c_{m-1}}\prod_j\mathrm{mult}_j(c_j)^{-1}\le c_{\mathrm{res}}^m\). Hence \(\mathrm{ss}_\xi\) is a combination of the \(\bigotimes_i\phi^{\mathrm{ev}}_i(\xi,c)\), over tuples \(c\) of cut points with representatives integral away from \(q\), with denominator \(1\) and size \(c_{\mathrm{res}}^m\).

Every prime dividing \(q_1\) splits in \(K\). Hence a prime \(p \ne d\) with \(\chi_K(p) \ne 1\) is prime to \(q_1\), and \([-p^e]\) is the place of the class of \(-p^e\).

Let \(p \ne d\) be inert in \(K\), \(\tau \in \Phi_a\), and suppose that \(\kappa([-p^e]\tau) = w\) for every positive odd integer \(e\). Then \(s_{\mathrm{fin},p}(a, \tau) = \sum_{e \ge 1,\ e\ \mathrm{odd}} (a/p^e - w)_+\), the first sum of Theorem 16.3.1 without the integer parts. Evaluated at \(p = 13\), \(a = 13^4\) and \(w = 1\), the sum is \(2208\).
Let \(p\) be prime and \(y \le a\). The terms of \(s_{\mathrm{fin}}(y, \sigma)\) with \(\nu\) a power of \(p\) add up to \(2\, s_{\mathrm{fin},p}(y, \sigma) \log p\).
Let \(\chi_K(p) \ne 1\) and let \((\tau, e)\) be a collision outside some \(\Phi'\). Then \(p \ne d\), \(e\) is odd, and \(o_p \mid e\); in particular \(o_p\) is odd.

Let \(q_0 = 18480\) and let \(p\) be a prime not dividing \(q_0\). If \(o_p\) is odd, then \(p \equiv -1 \pmod{240}\) and \(o_p \in \{1, 3, 5, 15\}\). For \(d = 138599\), the inert prime \(13\) has \(o_{13} = 20\). Among the primes inert in \({\mathbb{Q}}(\sqrt{-138599})\), the least with \(o_p\) odd is \(479\), with \(o_{479} = 15\), and the least with \(o_p = 1\) is \(55439\).
Let \(o \ge 0\) be an integer. If every collision \((\tau, e)\) outside \(\Phi'\) has \(e \ge o\), then \(C_p(\Phi') \le 2fa/p^o\).
Let \(p < x_1\) be a prime with \(\chi_K(p) \ne 1\) that is not exceptional. Then \(m\, C_p(\varnothing) \le L_p\).

Let \(p\) be exceptional with \(o_p = 1\), and let \(h_0 = \#({\mathbb{Z}}/q_0)^\times\). Then \(\#\Phi_a = f/h_0\) and \(m\, C_p(\varnothing) \ge m f a/(h_0 p)\), which exceeds \(L_p\) when \(m > h_0(\log b)^2\).

For a twist \(\vartheta\), a finitely supported \(\Psi\colon \mathcal T\to {\mathbb{C}}\) is a weak chain datum for \(\vartheta\) if: for every \(\mathfrak t\) in its support and every \(j\), the entries of \(\bar{\pi}_M\mathfrak t_j\) are integral at every finite place not dividing \(N \mathrm{Nm}\,Q_\vartheta\); every value \(\Psi(\mathfrak t)\) is integral under every ring map \({\mathbb{C}}\to {\mathbb{C}}_\ell\) for every prime \(\ell \nmid \mathrm{Nm}\,Q_\vartheta\); if \(Q_\vartheta = \varnothing\), then \(\sum_{\mathfrak t} \lvert\sigma(\Psi(\mathfrak t))\rvert \le \exp(x^{60})\) for every automorphism \(\sigma\) of \({\mathbb{C}}\); and \(\sum_{\mathfrak t} \Psi(\mathfrak t) \bigotimes_{j < m} v_j(\mathfrak t)\) is fixed by the levels of \(X_0, \dots, X_{m-1}\).

For a tame character \(\xi\) and a finitely supported \(\Psi\colon\mathcal T\to{\mathbb{C}}\), the restricted chain is \(R_{\xi,\Psi}:=\mathrm{res}\circ\bigl(\sum_{\mathfrak t}\Psi(\mathfrak t)\,\Theta^{\mathfrak t}_{m-1}\cdots\Theta^{\mathfrak t}_0\bigr)\) on \(S\), where \(\Theta^{\mathfrak t}_j\) is the definite lift from \(X_j\) to \(X_{j+1}\) of Definition 52.4.2, built from \(\xi\) with datum \(v_j(\mathfrak t)\), and \(\mathrm{res}\) is the restriction to \(Y_m\) of Definition 52.4.3.
