A descent pair \(\mathfrak{O}\) has two finitely indexed families of finite places of \(E\), chosen places and twist places; all their entries are distinct, and none is the conjugate of any entry. It has a hermitian space \(W\) of rank \(r'\) with signs on its basis indices and a specified adelic frame (Section 37.3) in which its Gram matrix is the diagonal matrix of the signs at every infinite place and the identity at every finite place, a function from the basis indices of \(W\) to the natural numbers, an injection of those indices into the basis indices of the standard definite space \(V = I_{n'}\) with \(r' < n'\) (its image is the set of selected indices), column multiplicities \(\beta^\pm(\tau,i)\) at each infinite place \(\tau\) and height \(i \ge 0\) (the diagrams of the weight, as in Definition 37.2.1), and a continuous unitary character \(\mu\) of \(U(1)(\mathbb A)\), trivial on rational points, with specified integral weight at each infinite place and specified tame part, a character \(\psi_w\) of \(k_w^\times\) at each finite place \(w\), trivial off the two families. Write \(K_0\) for the stabilizer of the standard integral lattice of \(V\) in the finite adelic group. The level of \(\mathfrak{O}\) consists of the elements of \(K_0\) whose reductions fix the selected basis vectors at the chosen places and preserve the span of the other basis vectors at the twist places. Its level character is the product over the twist places \(w\) of \(\psi_w^{-1}\) applied to the determinant of the block on the selected indices. Its forms \(\mathcal A(\mathfrak{O})\) are the algebraic forms on \(V\) on which the level acts through the level character, of the weight with column multiplicities \(\beta^+(\tau,i)+\beta^-(\tau,n'-i)\) at \(\tau\) and each height \(0\le i<n'\), and with determinant exponent \(-\sum_{1\le i<n'} \beta^-(\tau,i)\) at \(\tau\). We write \(t' := n' - r'\) for its rank difference.

Let \(e_1\) be an element of the complex group algebra of \(\prod_w \mathrm{GL}_{r'}(k_w)\) over the chosen places of \(\mathfrak{O}\), and \(A \subseteq \mathcal A(\mathfrak{O})\) a subspace. A tuple \(g = (g_w)_w\) of this group acts on \(\mathcal A(\mathfrak{O})\) by right translation by an element of \(K_0\) that reduces to \(\operatorname{diag}(g_w,1)\), in the order selected indices then complementary indices, at each chosen place \(w\), and to the identity at the twist places, multiplied by \(\prod_w \psi_w(\det g_w)\); write \(\mathrm{im}(e_1)\) for the image of the operator by which \(e_1\) then acts. In this sheet \(\upsilon_E\) is the splitting character of the Weil data on the ideles of \(E\) (Section 32.4), and \(\upsilon\) is its restriction to the norm-one ideles, as in Section 37.7. For a continuous unitary character \(a\) of the norm-one ideles of \(E\) that is trivial on the rational points of \(U(1)\), and a natural number \(N_0\ge 0\), the Frobenius value of \(a\) in rank \(N_0\) at a finite place \(w\) is \(q_w^{N_0/2}\) times the value, at the finite idele with the chosen uniformizer at \(w\) and \(1\) elsewhere, of the Hecke character \(x \mapsto a(x/\bar x)\,\upsilon_E(x)^{-N_0}\); here \(q_w = \#k_w\). For a split place \(w\) such that neither \(w\) nor \(\bar w\) is a place of \(\mathfrak{O}\), with the Hecke operators \(T_{w,i}\), \(0 \le i \le n'\), of Section 32.4 acting on \(\mathcal A(\mathfrak{O})\), the Hecke polynomial operator at \(w\) at the value \(T \in \mathbb{C}\) is \(\sum_{i=0}^{n'} (-T)^i q_w^{i(i-1)/2}\, T_{w,i}\). The false lifts at \(w\) are the forms in \(\mathrm{im}(e_1) \cap A\) killed by the Hecke polynomial operator of \(\mathfrak{O}\) at \(w\) at the value \(\bigl(\nu_w q_w^{n'-r'-1}\bigr)^{-1}\) expected of a lift, where \(\nu_w\) is the Frobenius value at \(w\) of \(\upsilon^{r_-}\) in rank \(r'\), with \(r_-\) the number of negative signs of \(W\). A form is orthogonal to the false lifts for \((\mathfrak{O}, e_1, A)\) if it is orthogonal to the false lifts at every such \(w\).

Let \(e_1\) be as in Definition 80.1.3, \(\mathcal F \subseteq \mathcal A(\mathfrak{O})\) a subspace, with orthogonal projection \(\mathrm{pr}\), and \(\mathrm{den} \in \mathbb R\). The projection onto \(\mathcal F\) has denominator at most \(\mathrm{den}\) at \(\iota\) if some operator \(C_\ell\) on \(\mathcal F\) has \(\lvert \iota(\det C_\ell) \rvert_\ell \ge \exp(-\dim \mathcal F \cdot r' \cdot \mathrm{den})\) and, for every form \(y\) integral at \(\iota\) and orthogonal to the false lifts for \((\mathfrak{O}, e_1, \mathcal F^\perp)\), \(C_\ell(\mathrm{pr}(y))\) is integral at \(\iota\) and \(\lvert \iota\langle C_\ell(\mathrm{pr}(y)), y' \rangle \rvert_\ell \le 1\) for every form \(y'\) integral at every ring map \(\mathbb{C}\to \mathbb{C}_\ell\). Here \(\langle\,,\rangle\) is the class sum of the pointwise Gram inner products, linear in the first variable; each term is weighted by the reciprocal of the order of the stabilizer of its double-coset representative.

The inverse avatar of a tame character \(\xi\) is the \(\ell\)-adic avatar \(\hat\xi \colon G_E \to \bar{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell^\times\), through \(\iota\), of the base change of \(\xi^{-1}\) to \(E\): the continuous character with \(\hat\xi(\mathrm{Art}\,x) = \iota\bigl(\xi(x/\bar x)\bigr)^{-1}\) for every finite idele \(x\) of \(E\), where \(\mathrm{Art}\) is the Artin map. We use the Artin map of the proof, with values in the topological abelianization \(G_E^{\mathrm{ab}}\) and with a local uniformizer mapping to geometric Frobenius modulo inertia. A character of \(G_E\) is evaluated there through the induced character. Let \(\mathrm{ram} \in [0, \infty]\). A twist \(\vartheta\) is auxiliary with ramification at most \(\mathrm{ram}\) (at \(\iota\)) if: every place of \(Q_\vartheta\) has prime norm, and neither it nor its conjugate divides \(\ell MN\) (its conjugate is not in \(Q_\vartheta\), as for every tame character); \(\hat\vartheta\) is locally constant, and there is a character \(\chi_0\) of the finite ideles of \(E\), with values in \(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell^\times\), such that \(\hat\vartheta(\mathrm{Art}\,x) = \chi_0(x/\bar x)\) for every finite idele \(x\), and \(\chi_0\) is trivial on \(E^\times\) and on every idele that is a unit at the places not above \(\ell\) and is congruent to \(1\) at the places of \(Q_\vartheta\); for some choice of a place of \(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}\) above each \(w \in Q_\vartheta\), with tame generators \(s_w\), \(\sum_{w \in Q_\vartheta} \operatorname{val}_+\bigl(\hat\vartheta(s_w) - 1\bigr) \le \mathrm{ram}\).
The trivial twist, with \(Q_\vartheta = \emptyset\), is auxiliary with ramification at most \(0\).

A descent pair \(\mathfrak{O}\) with a tuple of polynomials over the residue fields of its chosen places is in lift setting for \(\vartheta\) if its indexed chosen and twist places agree with those of the data and of \(\vartheta\); its tame part is the \(j\)-th power of the tame part of \(\chi_M\) from Section 37.7, times the tame part of \(\vartheta\), for some \(1 \le j \le m\); \(r'\) and \(n' - r'\) are odd, with \(r' \le r\) and \(n' - r' \le t\); each polynomial is a label of degree \(r'\) (Section 37.1), and none of its roots becomes \(1\) on multiplication by the element \(a_w\in k_w^\times\) defined as follows. Write \(T_w\) for the fixed injective character of \(\overline{k_w}^{\,\times}\) from Section 37.1 and \(\psi_w\) for the tame part at \(w\). Choose \(z_w\in k_w^\times\) with \(T_w(z_w)=\exp(2\pi i/(q_w-1))\). Then \(T_w(a_w)=\psi_w(z_w)^{-1}\). Finally, above each \(p_i\) one polynomial is irreducible with a root of order \((\#k_w)^{r} - 1\) (and then \(r' = r\)), or equal to \(X - 1\) with \(r' = 1\).

Let \(\vartheta\) be a twist, \(\mathfrak{O}\) a descent pair, \(e_1\) as in Definition 80.1.3, \(\mathcal F \subseteq \mathcal A(\mathfrak{O})\) a subspace and \(\mathrm{sel} \in [0, \infty]\). A lift generator for \((\vartheta, \mathfrak{O}, e_1, \mathcal F)\) with Selmer bound \(\mathrm{sel}\) is a form \(y \in \mathcal F\) such that: \(y\) lies in the range of the idempotent of a tuple of polynomials with which \(\mathfrak{O}\) is in lift setting for \(\vartheta\) (Definition 80.1.10), and the whole range of this idempotent is contained in \(\mathrm{im}(e_1)\); \(y\) lifts a family \(\mathfrak s\) for which there are a descent pair \(\mathfrak{O}_0\) with the same basis index sets for \(W\) and for \(V\) as \(\mathfrak{O}\), whose character \(\mu\) times \(\vartheta\) is that of \(\mathfrak{O}\), and a main summand \(R\) for \(\mathfrak{O}_0\) and \(\mathfrak s\) such that \(\hat\vartheta R\) has Selmer bound \(\mathrm{sel}\) (Definition 80.1.9).

Let \(\ell\) and \(\iota\) be as above, and let \(\vartheta\) be a twist that is auxiliary with ramification at most \(\mathrm{tw}_\ell\). Let \(\mathfrak{O}\) be a descent pair of ranks \(r' < n'\), \(e_1\) an element of the complex group algebra of \(\prod_w \mathrm{GL}_{r'}(k_w)\) over its chosen places, and \(\mathcal F \subseteq \mathcal A(\mathfrak{O})\) a subspace contained in the span of the lift generators for \((\vartheta, \mathfrak{O}, e_1, \mathcal F)\) with Selmer bound \(\mathrm{tw}_\ell\). Then the projection onto \(\mathcal F\) has denominator at most \(\mathrm{cl}_\ell \log \ell\) at \(\iota\), in the sense of Definition 80.1.4.

Let \(r', t'\) be integers with \(1 \le r' \le r\) and \(0 \le t' \le t\), and let \(0 \le \mathrm{sel}, \mathrm{ram} \le \mathrm{tw}_\ell\). Then \[\mathrm{sel} + 2t'\,\mathrm{ram} + r'\,\mathrm{loc}_\ell + \varepsilon_\ell + n_\ell \le r'\mathrm{cl}_\ell .\]
For \(r' = 1\), \(1 \le t' \le t\) and \(\mathrm{sel} = \mathrm{ram} = \mathrm{tw}_\ell\), the two sides of Problem 80.1.3 differ by exactly \(2(t - t')\,\mathrm{tw}_\ell\).

Let \(\mathcal F\) be a finite-dimensional complex vector space, \(n_0 \ge 0\) an integer, \(u_0\) a nonnegative real number, and \(C_\ell \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbb{C}}(\mathcal F)\) with \(\operatorname{val}_+(n_0\iota(\mu)) \le u_0\) for every eigenvalue \(\mu\) of \(C_\ell\). Then, with \(\lvert \ell \rvert_\ell = \ell^{-1}\), \(\lvert \iota(\det(n_0C_\ell)) \rvert_\ell \ge \exp(-\dim \mathcal F \cdot u_0 \log \ell)\).

The sum of \(2^{-\ell}\log \ell\) over all primes \(\ell\) is \(0.3776\ldots\), and for every finite set \(P_0\) of primes, \(\sum_{\ell \in P_0} \mathrm{tw}_\ell \log \ell \le (4f + 3)\,r \log \mathcal N + 0.378\).

Granting the five displayed inequalities, for every finite set \(P_0\) of primes \[\sum_{\ell \in P_0} \bigl(\mathrm{cl}_\ell + \operatorname{val}_\ell(C_1)\bigr)\log\ell \;\le\; 4\cdot 10^6 e^{180} f\,\frac mk\, b\log b + (1 + 2t)\,x^{999} + x^{4000} + \log\mathcal N + x^{30} \;\le\; B .\]

Hence, if \(\mathfrak f_A\) (\(A \subseteq \mathcal{K}\)) are operators with \(\mathfrak f_A = 0\) for \(A \ne \mathcal{K}\), then \(\sum_A \mathbf N_{\mathcal{K}\setminus A}\,\mathfrak f_A = \mathrm{Nm}_{\mathcal{K}} \mathfrak f_{\mathcal{K}}\).

Let a finite group \(H\) act on a finite set \(\Omega\), with stabilizer orders dividing \(n_{\mathrm{st}}\), and on functions \(\varphi \colon \Omega \to \mathbb{Z}\) by \((h\varphi)(x) := \varphi(h^{-1}x)\). There is a function \(\omega \colon \Omega \to \mathbb{Z}\) such that the operator \(\Psi\) of multiplication by \(\omega\) satisfies \(\sum_{h \in H} h^{-1}\Psi h = n_{\mathrm{st}}\). If \(H\) acts freely, \(\omega\) can be \(n_{\mathrm{st}}\) times the indicator of a set of orbit representatives.

For finitely many systems \(\pi_k\) that are not weak lifts choose \(g_k\) with \(b_k := \det(1 - U_{\pi_k}(g_k)) \ne 0\), and let \(\beta_k(\pi) := \det(1 - U_\pi(g_k))\) (in this sheet). Then \(\delta_0 := \prod_k(b_k - \beta_k)\) vanishes at every \(\pi_k\) and equals \(n_0 := \prod_k b_k\) at every weak lift. For the two classes at \(11\), over \(\mathbb{Q}\) with \(\ell = 5\), let \(g\) be an arithmetic Frobenius element at \(2\), \(U = 1 \oplus \chi_{\mathrm{cyc}}\) on the constant function (a weak lift) and \(U = \rho_{11}\) on \(\varphi_{11}\) (Problem 81.2.1), with \(\det\rho_{11} = \chi_{\mathrm{cyc}}\). For a nontrivial character \(\chi\) of \((\mathbb{Z}/u)^\times\) and a prime \(v \nmid u\), \(\chi(\theta^{\mathbb{Q}}_{uv}) = (1 - \chi(v)^{-1})\,\chi(\theta^{\mathbb{Q}}_u)\): an insertion identity with \(\alpha\) trivial, one sign and \(L = [0]\). A continuous cocycle of \(G_{\mathbb{Q}_{11}}\) with values in \(\mathbb F_5\) and trivial action is a homomorphism; it is trivial on wild inertia and is determined by its values \((a, b)\) at a Frobenius lift and at a generator of tame inertia, and all \(25\) pairs occur. For \(\chi_\zeta = \prod_{w} \zeta_w^{\lg_w}\) and \(n \ge 1\), \(\chi_\zeta^n = \prod_{w} (\zeta_w^n)^{\lg_w}\), and \(\chi_\zeta^{\ell^{h_1}} = 1\). For \(w \in Q\) some \(g\) in an inertia group at \(w\) has \(\chi_\zeta(g) = \zeta_w\).

Let \(0 < \rho < 1\) and \(m \ge 1\), and let the \(\zeta_w\), \(w \in Q\), be \(\ell^{h_1}\)-th roots of unity with \(\operatorname{val}(\zeta_w - 1) \le \rho/m\). Let \(0 < \varepsilon < 1\) and \(m \ge 1\). (twisting theorem). Let \(\iota\colon \mathbb{C}\simeq \bar{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell\), and let \(R_1, \dots, R_n\) (\(n \ge 0\); not to be confused with the ratios \(R_P\) of clause 3) be \(\ell\)-adic representations of \(G_E\) such that each \(R_i\) is main-summand-like for \((t'_i, \mathrm{HT}_i)\), for some integer \(t'_i \ge 0\) and some family \(\mathrm{HT}_i\) (Definition 80.1.7). For each \(R_i\) in Theorem 85.1.2, let \(T_{\mathrm{Sel}}\) be the datum supplied for \(R_i\) by Problem 90.4.1, with the bound of Theorem 90.3.1. Show that \(\mathrm{bd}(T_{\mathrm{Sel}}) + 2^{-\ell} \le \mathrm{tw}_\ell\).

Roots of unity for many polynomials

If \(h \ge 1\) and \(\zeta\) has order \(\ell^h\), then \(\operatorname{val}(\zeta - 1) = \rho_h\). For \(\ell = 3\) the radii \(\rho_1, \rho_2, \rho_3\) are \(1/2, 1/6, 1/18\); for \(\ell = 2\) they are \(1, 1/2, 1/4\). The \(\rho_h\) with \(h \ge 1\) are distinct and tend to \(0\).

Let \(0 \ne g \in \bar{\mathbb{Z}}_\ell[Y]\), and write \(g = c\prod_k (Y - \alpha_k)\) in \(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell[Y]\). For rational \(\rho \ge 0\), \[v_\rho(g) = \operatorname{val}(c) + \sum\nolimits_k \min\bigl(\operatorname{val}(\alpha_k), \rho\bigr).\] Hence \(v_\rho(g_1g_2) = v_\rho(g_1) + v_\rho(g_2)\), and \(\rho \mapsto v_\rho(g)\) is nondecreasing.

(a) If \(\operatorname{val}(x) \ge \rho\), then \(\operatorname{val}(g(x)) \ge v_\rho(g)\). (b) If \(\operatorname{val}(y) = \rho\), then \[\operatorname{val}(g(y)) = v_\rho(g) + \sum\nolimits_{\alpha \in R_\rho(g)} \bigl(\operatorname{val}(y - \alpha) - \rho\bigr).\]

Let \(\ell = 3\) and \(g = Y^2 + 3Y + 3\). Then \(v_\rho(g) = \min(1, 2\rho)\), and for \(\zeta\) of order \(3^h\) the valuation \(\operatorname{val}(g(\zeta - 1))\) is \(\infty\) if \(h = 1\) and \(2\rho_h = v_{\rho_h}(g)\) if \(h \ge 2\).

Let \(\delta > 0\) and \(\beta \ge 0\) (in this sheet \(\beta\) is a real bound), with \(\beta < \delta \sum_{h \in H(\rho, h_0)} 1/(h + 1)\). If \(v_\rho(g) \le \beta\), then some \(h \in H(\rho, h_0)\) has \(\# R_{\rho_h}(g) \cdot \rho_h \le \delta/(h + 1)\).

Let \(\alpha \in \bar{\mathbb{Z}}_\ell\) with \(\operatorname{val}(\alpha) > 0\), and \(h \ge 1\). Then \[\sum\nolimits_{\zeta} \min\bigl(\operatorname{val}(\zeta - 1 - \alpha), 1\bigr) \le h + 1,\] the sum over the \(\zeta\) of order \(\ell^h\). For \(\ell = 3\), \(h = 1\) and \(\alpha = \zeta_0 - 1\), with \(\zeta_0\) of order \(3\), the sum is \(3/2\).

For \(\ell = 3\), \(h = 2\) and \(\alpha = \zeta_9 - 1\), the six terms \(\min(\operatorname{val}(\zeta - 1 - \alpha), 1)\), for \(\zeta = \zeta_9^e\) with \(e = 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8\), are \(1, \tfrac16, \tfrac12, \tfrac16, \tfrac12, \tfrac16\); their sum is \(\tfrac52 \le h + 1\).

Let \(R\) be a finite multiset of elements of \(\bar{\mathbb{Z}}_\ell\) of positive valuation, and \(h \ge 1\). Some \(\zeta\) of order \(\ell^h\) has \(\sum_{\alpha \in R} \min\bigl(\operatorname{val}(\zeta - 1 - \alpha), 1\bigr) \le \#R \cdot \rho_h (h + 1)\).

Let \(0 < \delta < 1\), \(\rho > 0\) rational, and \(\beta < \delta\sum_{h \in H(\rho, h_0)} 1/(h + 1)\). If \(v_\rho(g) \le \beta\), then for some \(h \in H(\rho, h_0)\) and some \(\zeta\) of order \(\ell^h\), \[\operatorname{val}\bigl(g(\zeta - 1)\bigr) \le v_{\rho_h}(g) + \delta .\]

For rational \(\rho > 0\), real \(\delta > 0\) and \(\beta \ge 0\), some \(h_0\) has \(\beta < \delta\sum_{h \in H(\rho, h_0)} 1/(h + 1)\). For \(\ell = 2\), \(\rho = \delta = 1/2\) and \(\beta = 1\), the least such \(h_0\) is \(18\).

Let \(\delta\), \(\rho\), \(\beta\), \(h_0\) be as in Problem 86.1.10. If \(\operatorname{val}(x) \ge \rho\) and \(\operatorname{val}(g(x)) \le \beta\), then some \(\zeta\) with \(\zeta^{\ell^{h_0}} = 1\) and \(\operatorname{val}(\zeta - 1) \le \rho\) has \(\operatorname{val}(g(\zeta - 1)) \le \operatorname{val}(g(x)) + \delta\).

Fix \(j \in \mathcal V\), and assume \(\operatorname{val}(x_{ij}) \ge \rho\) for all \(i\) (the other coordinates are only integral). Let \(0 < \delta < 1\), \(\beta < \delta\sum_{h \in H(\rho, h_0)} 1/(h + 1)\), and \(\sum_i \operatorname{val}(F_i(x_i)) \le \beta\). There is \(\zeta\) with \(\zeta^{\ell^{h_0}} = 1\) and \(\operatorname{val}(\zeta - 1) \le \rho\) such that, if the coordinate \(x_{ij}\) is replaced by \(\zeta - 1\) for every \(i\), each \(\operatorname{val}(F_i(x_i))\), and also their sum, grows by at most \(\delta\).

Let \(0 < \delta < 1\), \(\#\mathcal V \cdot \delta \le 1\), \(\beta + 1 < \delta\sum_{h \in H(\rho, h_0)} 1/(h + 1)\), \(\operatorname{val}(x_{ij}) \ge \rho\) for all \(i, j\), and \(\sum_i \operatorname{val}(F_i(x_i)) \le \beta\). There are \(\zeta_j\), \(j \in \mathcal V\), with \(\zeta_j^{\ell^{h_0}} = 1\), \(\operatorname{val}(\zeta_j - 1) \le \rho\), and \(\operatorname{val}\bigl(F_i((\zeta_j - 1)_j)\bigr) \le \operatorname{val}(F_i(x_i)) + \#\mathcal V\cdot\delta\) for all \(i\).

Let \(\ell = 3\), \(F_1 = X + Y\), \(F_2 = XY + 3\), \(F_3 = X^2 + 3X + 3\), with starting points \((3, 0)\), \((0, 3)\), \((0, 0)\), at which each \(F_i\) has valuation \(1\). For \(\zeta = \zeta_{27}\), the common point \((\zeta - 1, \zeta^2 - 1)\) gives \(\operatorname{val}(F_i) = \tfrac19\) for \(i = 1, 2, 3\).

Let \(s_0 \ge 0\) be an integer, \(\rho > 0\) rational, \(\beta \ge 0\) and \(\varepsilon > 0\). There is \(h_0\) with the following property. Let \(\mathcal V\), \(I\) be finite sets with \(\#\mathcal V \le s_0\), let \(F_i \in \bar{\mathbb{Z}}_\ell[X_j : j \in \mathcal V]\) and \(x_i \in \bar{\mathbb{Z}}_\ell^\mathcal V\) for \(i \in I\), with \(\operatorname{val}(x_{ij}) \ge \rho\) for all \(i, j\) and \(\sum_i \operatorname{val}(F_i(x_i)) \le \beta\). Then there are \(\zeta_j \in \bar{\mathbb{Z}}_\ell\), \(j \in \mathcal V\), with \[\zeta_j^{\ell^{h_0}} = 1,\quad \operatorname{val}(\zeta_j-1)\le\rho \quad(j\in\mathcal V),\qquad \operatorname{val}\bigl(F_i((\zeta_j-1)_j)\bigr) \le \operatorname{val}\bigl(F_i(x_i)\bigr)+\varepsilon \quad(i\in I).\]

Let \(n \ge 1\) and \(x \in \bar{\mathbb{Z}}_\ell\) with \(\operatorname{val}(x) \ge \rho\). Some \(x' \in \bar{\mathbb{Z}}_\ell\) has \((1 + x')^n = 1 + x\) and \(\operatorname{val}(x') \ge \rho/n\).

Let \(0 < \rho < 1\), \(1 \le n \le m\), and let \(\zeta\) have \(\ell\)-power order and \(\operatorname{val}(\zeta - 1) \le \rho/m\). Then \(\operatorname{val}(\zeta^n - 1) \le \rho\); in particular \(\zeta^n \ne 1\). For \(\ell = 2\), \(\zeta\) of order \(8\), \(m = n = 2\) and \(\rho = 1/2\), equality holds.

Let \(\ell = 3\) and \(\Phi_3(Y) = Y^2 + Y + 1\). The values \(\operatorname{val}(\Phi_3(\zeta_n^j))\) for \(j = 1, 2, 3\) are \(\tfrac13, \tfrac13, \infty\) for \(n = 9\); \(\tfrac19, \tfrac19, \tfrac13\) for \(n = 27\); and \(\tfrac1{27}, \tfrac1{27}, \tfrac19\) for \(n = 81\). Let \(\ell = 3\) and \(X \in \mathbb{Z}_3\). The solutions \(u \in \mathbb{Z}/9\) of \(Xu = 0\) number \(9, 3, 9, 1\) for \(X = 0, 3, 9, 1\), and form a module of length \(\min(2, \operatorname{val}(X))\). The solutions \((u, u') \in (\mathbb{Z}/9)^2\) of \(Xu + u' = 0\), \(Xu' = 0\) number \(9, 9, 1\) for \(X = 0, 3, 1\), and form a module of length \(\min(2, 2\operatorname{val}(X))\).

Let \(\mathcal{O}'\) be a discrete valuation ring, \(0 \ne a \in \mathcal{O}'\), and \(A\) a matrix over \(\mathcal{O}'\) with \(n\) columns and any set of rows. Let \(A_a\) be \(A\) with the \(n\) rows of \(a I_n\) added. Then the length of the \(\mathcal{O}'\)-module \(\{u \in (\mathcal{O}'/a)^n : Au = 0\}\) is the least \(\mathrm{ord}_{\mathcal{O}'}(P)\), for \(P\) running over the \(n \times n\) minors of \(A_a\). For the two systems of Problem 87.1.1, with \(a = 9\), the sets of minors are \(\{X, 9\}\) and, up to sign, \(\{X^2, 9, 9X, 0, 81\}\).

Let \(\mathcal{O}\) be a coefficient ring, \(Q\) a finite set, \(A\) a matrix with \(n\) columns and entries in \(\mathcal{O}[X_w : w \in Q]\), \(0 \ne a \in \mathcal{O}\), and \(\mathcal D\) the set of \(n \times n\) minors of \(A_a\); they are polynomials. For a point \(x\) with coordinates in a coefficient ring \(\mathcal{O}' \supseteq \mathcal{O}\) let \(Z(x) := \{u \in (\mathcal{O}'/a)^n : A(x)u = 0\}\). (a) The normalized length of \(Z(x)\) is \(\min_{P \in \mathcal D} \operatorname{val}(P(x))\), and it is at most \(n \operatorname{val}(a)\). (b) Every \(P \in \mathcal D\) bounds the normalized length of \(Z(x)\) by \(\operatorname{val}(P(x))\) at every point \(x\); we say \(P\) is sharp at \(x_0\) if equality holds there. A minor sharp at one point therefore computes the length there and bounds it everywhere. (c) For \(\ell = 3\), \(Xu = 0\) and \(a = 9\): the minor \(9\) is sharp at \(X = 0\) and the minor \(X\) at \(X = 3\); the latter bounds the length at \(X = \zeta - 1\), \(\zeta\) of order \(9\), by \(1/6\).

A finite set \(Q\) of finite places of \(E\) is admissible for \(\Sigma_0\) if its places have prime norm, and \(Q\), its conjugate \(\bar Q\) and \(\Sigma_0\) are pairwise disjoint. A character for \(Q\) is a locally constant character \(\chi\colon G_E\to\bar{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell^\times\) for which there is a character \(\chi_0\) of the finite ideles of \(E\), trivial on the principal ideles and on every idele that is a unit at the places not above \(\ell\) and congruent to \(1\) at the places of \(Q\) not above \(\ell\), with \(\chi(\mathrm{Art}\,y)=\chi_0(y/\bar y)\) for every finite idele \(y\); here \(\mathrm{Art}\) is the Artin map of Definition 80.1.5. The same definition is used for homomorphisms to the additive group \(\mathbb{Z}/\ell^{h}\). Let \(h_1 \ge 1\) and, for each \(w \in Q\), let \(\lg_w \colon G_E \to \mathbb{Z}/\ell^{h_1}\) be a locally constant homomorphism; write \([n] \in \{0, \dots, \ell^{h_1} - 1\}\) for the representative of \(n \in \mathbb{Z}/\ell^{h_1}\). For \(\ell^{h_1}\)-th roots of unity \(\zeta_w\) and for variables \(X_w\) put \[\chi_\zeta(g) := \prod_{w \in Q} \zeta_w^{[\lg_w(g)]}, \qquad \chi_X(g) := \prod_{w \in Q} (1 + X_w)^{[\lg_w(g)]} \in \mathbb{Z}[X_w : w \in Q] .\]

(a) At \(X_w = \zeta_w - 1\) the polynomial \(\chi_X(g)\) takes the value \(\chi_\zeta(g)\); \(\chi_\zeta\) is a character of \(G_E\), and \(\chi_\zeta^n = \chi_{\zeta^n}\) for \(n \ge 1\), where \(\zeta^n := (\zeta_w^n)_w\). (b) For \(g, h \in G_E\), \(\chi_X(gh) - \chi_X(g)\chi_X(h)\) lies in the ideal generated by the \((1 + X_w)^{\ell^{h_1}} - 1\), \(w \in Q\).

Let \(\ell = 5\), and let \(G\) be the group of order \(100\) generated by \(g_1, \gamma, s\) with \(g_1^5 = \gamma^4 = s^5 = 1\), \(\gamma g_1 \gamma^{-1} = g_1^2\) and \(s\) central. Let \(\zeta_5\) be a root of unity of order \(5\), \(\mathcal{O}' = \mathbb{Z}_5[\zeta_5]\) and \(B = \mathcal{O}'/5\), and let \(i \in \mathbb{Z}_5\) be the fourth root of unity with \(i \equiv 2 \pmod 5\). For \(0 \le j \le 4\) let \(G\) act on \(B\) by the scalars \(g_1 \mapsto 1\), \(\gamma \mapsto i\), \(s \mapsto \zeta_5^j\). The cocycles \(z \colon G \to B\) with \(z(\gamma) = 0\) are determined by \(u = z(g_1)\), and they are the \(u\) with \((\zeta_5^j - 1)u = 0\). They number \(625, 5, 5, 5, 5\) for \(j = 0, \dots, 4\); the normalized length is \(\min(1, \operatorname{val}(\zeta_5^j - 1)) = 1, \tfrac14, \tfrac14, \tfrac14, \tfrac14\). With \(1 + X\) for the scalar of \(s\), the minors of Problem 87.1.3 for the equation \(Xu = 0\) on \(B\) are \(X\) and \(5\).

Let a group \(G\) act linearly on a module \(B\) over a commutative ring, and let \(\gamma \in G\) act by a scalar \(\lambda\) with \(\lambda - 1\) invertible. Every cocycle \(G \to B\) is, in exactly one way, the sum of a coboundary \(g \mapsto gb - b\) and a cocycle vanishing at \(\gamma\).

Let \(\mathcal{O}'\) be a coefficient ring, \(c \ge 1\) an integer, and \(Z\) an \(\mathcal{O}'\)-module in which every element is killed by a power of \(\ell\). If the submodule \(Z[\ell^c]\) of elements killed by \(\ell^c\) has normalized length less than \(c\), then \(Z = Z[\ell^c]\). For \(\ell = 3\), \(Z = \mathbb{Z}/27\) over \(\mathbb{Z}_3\) and \(c = 2\): \(Z[9]\) has \(9\) elements and length \(2\), and \(Z \ne Z[9]\).

Let \(\mathcal{O}\) be a coefficient ring. A Selmer datum for \((\Sigma_0, g_0)\) over \(\mathcal{O}\) is a free \(\mathcal{O}\)-module \(T_{\mathrm{Sel}}\) of finite rank \(\operatorname{rk}T_{\mathrm{Sel}}\ge 1\) with a continuous \(\mathcal{O}\)-linear action of \(G_E\), unramified outside a set \(\Sigma(T_{\mathrm{Sel}}) \subseteq \Sigma_0\) containing the places above \(\ell\); write \(T_{\mathrm{Sel}}(g)\) for the action of \(g\). The endomorphisms \(T_{\mathrm{Sel}}(g)\), \(g \in G_E\), span \(\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal{O}}(T_{\mathrm{Sel}})\) over \(\mathcal{O}\). For each finite place \(w\) of \(E\) fix a place of \(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}\) above \(w\), and write \(G_w\) for its decomposition group. For each \(w \mid \ell\) the datum supplies a finitely generated \(\mathcal{O}\)-module \(\mathcal Z_w\) of cocycles \(G_w \to T_{\mathrm{Sel}}\) containing the coboundaries, with \(\sum_{w \mid \ell}(\operatorname{rk}\mathcal Z_w - \operatorname{rk}T_{\mathrm{Sel}}) \le f_E \operatorname{rk}T_{\mathrm{Sel}}\), where \(f_E\) is the number of infinite places of \(E\). The local relations at \(w\) are the relations \(\sum_j a_j z(g_j) = 0\), with finitely many \(g_j \in G_w\) and \(a_j \in \operatorname{End}_{\mathcal{O}}(T_{\mathrm{Sel}})\), satisfied by all \(z \in \mathcal Z_w\). The datum also supplies an element \(\gamma(T_{\mathrm{Sel}})\) of inertia at a place of \(\Sigma(T_{\mathrm{Sel}})\) prime to \(\ell\) and a scalar \(\lambda \in \mathcal{O}\) with \(\lambda^2 - 1 \in \mathcal{O}^\times\); both \(\gamma(T_{\mathrm{Sel}})\) and \((\gamma(T_{\mathrm{Sel}})^c)^{-1}\) act on \(T_{\mathrm{Sel}}\) by \(\lambda\). A datum has three terms, in the nonnegative extended integers.
